body: Visiting Pedro Tea Factory was one of the most eye-opening and meaningful experiences of our trip.It is located just a short five-minute drive from Nuwara Eliya town, making it very easy to reach. A helpful tip, if you are planning to combine this with a visit to Lover’s Leap Waterfall, make sure you wear proper footwear, as the terrain can be uneven and more like a short hike.The visit itself was well organised. There was plenty of parking, and the check-in process was straightforward. We were warmly welcomed at the visitors’ centre, and the entry fee of Rs.1000 per person (above 11 years) felt very reasonable for the experience.We spent around 15 minutes taking in the surroundings and reading about the history of the plantation before our guided tour began. Our guide was excellent, knowledgeable, engaging, and clearly very experienced. She shared that her connection to the factory goes back several generations, which really showed in the depth of her knowledge and pride in the work.The tour takes you through the full journey of tea, from leaf picking to processing, grading, and eventually reaching the Colombo Tea Auction. Seeing each stage in person gives you a completely different appreciation for what goes into something as simple as a cup of tea.It really makes you stop and think. Back in the UK, it is easy to pick up a box of tea bags for a couple of pounds without a second thought. But here, you see the effort, skill, and dedication of the people behind it. The men and women working in the plantation and factory put in an incredible amount of hard work to produce something we often take for granted.This visit genuinely changed the way I see tea. Every cup now feels more meaningful. From the highest tea plantations in Sri Lanka to a cup in your hand, it is a long journey that deserves respect.If you are in the area, I would strongly recommend visiting. It is not just a tour, it is an experience that gives you a deeper appreciation for one of the world’s most loved drinks. And if you can, choose Ceylon tea, it supports the people and communities who work so hard to produce it.Ps: your wait is worth after the tour you are offered a freshly brewed cup of tea, it is indeed heavenly.
title: A powerful reminder behind every cup of tea

body: Definitely one of the best teas in Sri Lanka. Very attentive to sustainability.A tour with tasting not to be missed.
title: Tea for two

body: Had a great experience . Wonderful day and great fun. A wide variety of items. Good explanation of all the different types of items
title: Great adventure

body: Poor service, we waited 20 min at the door for someone to even speak to us about a tour. The “tour” we did was tea plucking, she told us what leaves were picked in less than 1 minute and then we plucked a few and left. It was not at all a good experience. Yesterday we went to labookalie and it was a MUCH better experience.
title: Don’t bother

body: Did both factory and picking tour (1000 rp each). Factory not working Sunday and no pickers because of wind, however an excellent tour ... very good English. Tea tasting was a single cup, but very nice. Picking was fun and got some good photos. Very close to Nuwara Eliya and lovers leap waterfall
title: Nice tour, ,lovely staff

body: Having visited a working factory previously , I was disappointed to pay 1000 Rupees each person to wait for a group to form then start the visit. No photos allowed inside the factory.The girl gave good explanation but at times it was difficult to hear what she said. Only the fanning was working when the tea leaves separated debris thus dusts on the floor and staff cleaning machines. Only worth buying Pedro tea as nowhere else sells it ! 95 % for export and only 5 % probably in the shop . It’s the tea brits drink under different names!
title: Ok if you never visited a tea factory but staff would have finished work so machineries will be silent and place empty .

body: We really enjoyed the tour, the lady gave us lots of information as we went around the factory. You get a cup of tea afterwards, which was enjoyed looking out from their terrace across the tea estate, which was stunning. Recommended.
title: Well worth a visit

body: We were recommended to visit early as the tea processing happens overnight. The visitor centre opens at 8 am. We had an excellent tour at 8.30am with Kaushi. The cutting machines and sorting machines were still working. Sadly no photos are allowed inside the factory which is such a shame. The tour took about 20 mins and was really informative. Then we were given a cup of tea on the balcony overlooking the plantation. We also paid another 1000 rupees for the plucking tour. This was very disappointing and not worth the money. Kaushi gave us bags to wear and took us out to the tea plantation. She explained how the pluckers work, selecting one bud and two leaves and then said we had 20 minutes to pick tea ourselves. We decided against that, instead walking to photograph some of the tea pluckers. Of course they wanted to be reimbursed for having their photos taken, so have plenty of small notes and wear sturdy shoes!
title: Go early to see the factory working

body: Great factory to visit. Set in a very scenic location. The lady giving the tour was excellent - she answered all my questions and provided us with plenty of information. Highly recommended
title: Great tour of a Tea Factory

body: Extremely Disappointed – Not Worth the Money!Pedro Tea Factory is an absolute rip-off! They charge 1000 rupees just for a basic factory visit – no complimentary tea, no plantation walk, nothing extra. That price is outrageous considering other tea factories in the area offer much better service and a more immersive experience for half the price or even free.On top of that, the staff were shockingly rude and unwelcoming. They clearly don’t care about tourists or customer service. It felt like we were an inconvenience to them.There are plenty of other tea factories in Nuwara Eliya that are far more worth your time and money. Don’t waste either of those at Pedro. Highly disappointing.
title: Not worth the money at all

body: Dreadful tour. Charged 1k rupees to be show around the factory by someone that couldn’t be bothered. The staff were less than impressed that we had chosen their tour above all others. Don’t waste your time, here are many tours to go on and I wish we had picked a different one.
title: Not worth the time and money

body: Over priced and completely commercial. Moreover there is nothing to see in the factory or the lounge. Over hyped. Arrogant staff.
title: Better to go to DAMRO

body: The factory tour is actually much shorter than I expected.I had difficulty hearing what the tour guide was saying as a lot of background noise .Given a cup of tea to sample at end of tour. Teas in the shop are very expensive.Please note lots of steps up and down during the factory tour - not the easiest.
title: Short tour .

body: We had an excellent walk up to this place from our hotel at the quiet end of the lake. It's a peaceful walk (more interesting than tuktuk) We didn't do the tea factory tour but enjoyed a free cuppa overlooking the beautiful tea gardens and bought tea that was surprisingly well priced compared to the previous tea factory we visited. We then took a gorgeous walk up to lovers leap waterfall. Highly recommended. NB get the bus back into town from here,it's cheap as chips and do walk up to the waterfall the views are stunning
title: Good tea in a beautiful setting

body: This wasn't a planned visit...on our way back from Lover's Leap our tuk driver suggested a visit to take part in their factory tour.... even though we've done this a couple of times before we thought why not and proceeded....And it turned out be the best tea factory tour we've had so far! It was a precise and concise tour of 20 mts where they take you through each division of the factory while explaining the tea making process from end to end. And it was also the most informative of all the tea factory tours we've had so far.The lady who did the tour did an excellent job. She was very knowledgeable and answered many questions. We went there around 10.30 am and immediately joined a tour that was just about to start. After the tour you get a nice cup of tea. (I think there are tours every half an hour.) If you arrive while a tour is ongoing they will serve you tea first which you can enjoy in their tea lounge while enjoying the lovely view. We paid LKR 500 each and I think it was the same for locals and foreigners. No photos or videos are allowed inside the factory. [If I am nitpicking, the aprons they provide visitors to wear during the tour can do with a makeover.]We Also learnt that the name of the Estate is pronounced as "Peedro" (not "Pedro") same as how the British colonists called "Piduruthalaga" the highest mountained "Mount Pedro", pronounced as "Mount Peedro".The factory is quite close to Nuwara Eliya town. Road conditions are good. It's on the side of the Udupussellawa road and there is ample parking inside the property. They also have a collection of single estate tea for sale.If you are interested in touring a tea factory and learning about the tea making process I would highly recommend this tour.
title: The tale of tea making

body: We had a four-person lead with another couple. The employee guided us in the fast-track max. 15 minutes through the factory. She spoke very good English, but she rattled down the information as if memorized, so you could hardly follow. In the end, there was no tea tasting, the real reason we had visited the factory in the first place. On request, it was said that there were currently no more samples. Milk was also no longer in stock. Too bad!
title: Don't expect too much!

body: Entrance costs 1,000 rupees per person, the tour is very short, about 15 minutes, and you can only see the machines themselves but you can't see the creature itself because it only happens at night.There's a feeling that the tour was done in an area only for tours and that they don't show the factory itself. The machines they look very dusty and outdated, really feel like a fake representative.
title: Disappointed

body: We loved the explanation as part of the tea factory visit, they charged us 500LKR per person for the tour however we weren’t told the factory is under renovation. There was construction and civil work happening inside the factory and we couldn’t see the entire process. When I made the suggestion to the front desk staff that they could have told us about the work happening inside, they said yes reluctantly! Cup of tea served after the tour was delicious.
title: Check if the factory is functional before you pay for the visit!

body: Definitely not worth the detour. Totally selfless guide. Quick visit. Very little explanation. We waited 1/2 hour before being picked up. She blocked us at the entrance on the way back... plus the tea is horribly expensive.
title: Bad

body: We were staying in Nuwara Eliya for a couple of days and wanted to visit a tea plantation and this was recommended by the hotel (Grand). We took a Tuk-tuk from the hotel and the driver waited for us while we did the tour (approx 45 minutes in total including time to drink and buy tea).Very informative tour with a chance to see production from start to end with a good tour guide who was keen to answer questions. Great selection of tea to buy with a good explanation of what you are buying. We brought lots back.This felt like a much more local experience than the commercial plantation that we stopped at on our way out of Nuwara.So would definitely recommend this - local, less expensive and felt a bit more real.
title: Well worth a visit and easy to get to if you're in Nuwara

body: Nice place, pleasant and very professional guidance, kind. Lovely. Indulging in a cup of tea 🍵, relatively expensive but special shop, worth a visit, spectacular view
title: Worth a visit

body: We really do not recommend this plan for tourists. No welcome, they left us waiting without any information for 1/2 hour. Not enough staff to receive customers.The visit to the factory is uninteresting, not sufficiently supported, sloppy. The guide repeats the same information over and over again without answering the questions asked. Don't waste your time, look elsewhere, another area.
title: Tourist trap, avoid!!

body: Great experience. 500LKR/pax for an interesting tour around the tea factory (photos prohibited) and a complimentary cup of tea. 1000LKR/pax to have a practical demo of tea picking, and 15/20 minutes to try it out yourself. 1100LKR/pax for tea tasting.Overall, a cheap and fun afternoon out!
title: Cheap and fun afternoon out

body: We did a short tour here. I enjoyed seeing the old factory and old machines that are all still in use. You can see some old photos as well of important people who have visited over the years. A good explanation of how tea is made. A nice cuppa at the end as well.
title: Good short tour

body: The young lady guide was pleasant but the factory tour showed how many manual processes are yet to be automated.The newest machines seemed to be from 1986.As the factory operates between midnight and 0600 hours when the area is at its coolest, all we could watch was a couple of workers separating picked tea leaves as well as others carrying heavy bundles between sites.Some visitors went down a hill to see how an employee picks the leaves. It needs skill, and constant avoidance of thorns. Not a job I'd have ever enjoyed, especially given the midday heat. The gift shop was the focus of the estate. Along with a cup of tea it concluded the experience.
title: Pleasant cup of tea at conclusion

body: We were staying local to Pedro Tea Estate and visited one afternoon. Firstly we were offered free roaming of the tea plantation and walked down to near the lake, then had a complimentary tea & a tour. Hashini was very knowledgeable & explained the process very well. Photos were not allowed inside however the outside was very scenic.At the end, you could buy some of the tea made, which I assume is where revenue comes in. Overall I’d definitely recommend this experience!
title: A good experience from an avid tea fan

body: For us, however, it was a beautiful experience: the plantation tries to respect ethics and sustainability criteria and for this reason it differs from the others. We visited the factory with the original 19th century machinery still working and the explanation was concise but exhaustive. At the end they offered us an excellent cup of tea, accompanied by a freshly fried spicy 'rollo': delicious.
title: Sui generis but 5 stars

body: The factory tour was very quick and it was difficult to hear what the guide was saying. Explanations (what we heard) were exceptionally brief and we were not allowed to really look at the process or take photographs.
title: Underwhelming experience

body: Unlike the Damro plantation you have to pay for a factory tour - which wasn’t actually productive at the time of our visit , just running the sizing side of the process. We waited an age in the foyer for any instructions on where and when the tour would start. The lady who finally showed up led us off in too large a group size - such that only those directly next to her could hear her.
title: A bit disorganised, really focused on the shop sales

body: At first glance, the place looks nice except that the factory tour costs 500 RPS,If you want to see the tea fields and pick a little you will need to add 1000 rpsThen if you want to taste a tea even a little to know what you are buying you will have to add 1100 rpsAll done in a clearly expeditious manner,Visit to the factory (20 mins),For the collection, we give you a bag, we tell you: you go there, you pick it up, you have 20 minutes and I will come back to pick you up!The store... No possibility of buying an individual box, there are only packs of 6 for the price of 6500 rps...No authenticity... Disappointed!!!
title: Move on, money pump!!!

body: They take you on a short tour of their tea factory and plantation. You have to pay a fee for the tour. You will to taste the tea grown there
title: Plantation tour

body: You can visit wonderful tea gardens and taste tea. There are short tours in the factory where you can see the tea production step by step, and there is a free tea tasting at the end of the tour. There is also a sales office where you can buy gift tea.
title: Amazing experience

body: Very disappointing visit lasting 10 minutes for a cost of 500 rupees.We visited with a couple who had been to other much nicer free tea factories.Incomplete visit
title: Incomplete visit

body: We bought 2 tickets for factory visit and the tea collection, entire tour was super unorganized, lady who has provided the factory tour did the tour with unprofessional attitude as if she was forced to give us a tour; no communication whatsoever when we reached back to the main entrance. Then she gave us the baskets and told us to walk in the garden… then the toilets (female) were disgustingly dirty; flush was not working either. I would not do it or recommend it to any of my friends.
title: Disappointed

body: Don’t go on Saturday. There’s nobody working. The tour is done in 10 minutes (does not include the fields, just the factory) and the price is not worthy (at least at the weekend). I have visited other tea factories for free and you just pay for what you buy. Here we were charged 500LKR per person for practically nothing. A waste of money and time during the weekend.
title: Don’t go on Saturday

body: The visit was hasty, the explanation in English difficult to understand from a rather rude companion.It is also the only tea factory and plantation where an entrance fee of 500 rupees is required.At the end you can make purchases in the shop.If you want to visit a plantation there are better solutions in the area, much larger and free.
title: Disappointing

body: As we already did a tea factory tour at another site on the way to Nuwara Eliya, we decided to only do the Tea plucking for 2k Rupees on the Pedro Estate. We actually hoped for some explanation or that they would weigh the leaves we picked afterwards, but it was really just handing out the cappy-held baskets (which smelled like old sweat btw) and nothing more. The field next to the site is nice to take some pictures, but we really had hoped for more than just this.
title: No explanations, just tourist exploiting

body: Pedro Tea Factory is a reasonably small facility, but located on their Lovers Leap tea estate, just minutes from Nuwara Eliya township, so reasonably easy to visit. The factory tour takes about 20 minutes and costs 500 LKR per person. Most of the machinery in the factory was sitting idle, but our guide said that the processing was done at night due to the different humidity and drying qualities. A number of reviewers have said how informative their tour was, but that wasn't the case with ours. Our tour guide was quite unengaged. The tour felt rushed, she parroted a few facts quickly and quietly in each room of the factory, and was very difficult to hear or understand. I don't think anyone on our tour came away with much more knowledge on tea production than they went in with. You weren't permitted to take photos in rooms with grading equipment. The reception area of the tours was modern, with a balcony overlooking a small tea planting. There were a few women plucking leaves below the balcony, but they appeared to be doing it primarily as a photo opportunity for tour participants. There is also a walking track to Lovers Leap Waterfall from the factory site.
title: Tour quality depends on your guide.

body: The visit at Pedro Estate was so nice. We could take a walk through the beautiful garden, taste delicious black tea and got a very interesting tour through the factory.
title: So recommendable!

body: We had a four here with tea tasting at the end. It’s an eye opener to what the ladies experience during their working hours in the factory especially in the drying room which is extremely hot! Tour guide was brilliant and very informative. Tea tasted so good had to buy some!
title: Great tour

body: This tour is quite dull. It only took about 10 minutes, and no photos are allowed. If it was a free tour, it would be fine, but I'm not sure it's worth paying for.We saw the tea factory at the Heritance Tea Factory hotel- it was free, and much better.
title: Maybe not the best factory tour.

body: Nice tea estate and one of the oldest. Tour of the factory is not free. There are other 2 tea factories in Nuwara Eliya , which I believe are better in terms of service.Staff seemed to be least interested in selling the products, which is unusual for Sri Lanka.
title: Can be avoided as other options are better

body: We intended to go on a factory tour, but they told us the factory wasn’t running at the moment. We decided to do a tea tasting instead. 6 cups of tea were put in front of us without any explanation.. I then asked someone for an explanation, she just told me which cup was which tea, no further explanation.
title: No explanation

body: This is where we purchase our tea from every time we visit Nuwara Eliya. We have visited Pedro tea factory over 5 times now. This was our 7 month old's first time though. The tea is superb and the view of the tea plantations from the viewing deck is a nice experience. We did experience the factory tour once which was very informative. Highly recommended for a nice experience if you enjoy Ceylon Tea.
title: Nice Experience in the Tea Factory

body: Impressive to see all the tea plantations in Nuwara eliya, which are very big. We had a very good tour guide who showed us the factory and explained the process of making tea very clear. Also very impressive to see under which circumstances the employees live.
title: Beautiful tea estate

body: Lovely old tea factory in the hills. we were given a tour of the factory and shown how the leaves are processed. At the end we got to taste 2 kinds of tea. The tea is brewed for exactly 5 minutes.
title: Lovely old tea factory

body: I only ever leave reviews when things are really good, or very bad and this was very VERY BAD. We had wanted to do the factory tour and were told on our arrival that we weren’t able to because the factory wasn’t open for visitors that day (oddly). We were told that the only two activities we could do where the two (more expensive at 1100 Rs pp) “experiences” of Tea tasting or Tea picking; we opted for the tea tasting. We said we understood that the factory was closed for tours but asked if it would be possible to pop our heads round to see the inside of the factory? The woman said yes. So we sat down for our tea tasting, and after 10 minutes a tray of tea was plonked in front of us, a different woman pointed and said some teas were strong and others weren’t, and then departed(!) There was no explanation about the variations of tea on the tray, how they are grown, or what they were even! Nothing. Nada. We were just left to our tray of random teas. It was an absolute joke. We tried to find someone to ask questions but got minimal information and no actual explanation on the process. We then said asked if we could have a quick look round the door at the factory, and the woman in charge said “yes that’s fine, that’ll be Rs.350 each” i.e. the cost of the tour which we had initially asked for and were told that we couldn’t do!! I queried why we were told merely 15 minutes earlier that we couldn’t do the tour of the tea factory, at which point the woman basically lied to us and claimed she had included it as an option!! She was basically scoffing at us as she spoke implying that all 3 of us had misunderstood. The Sri Lankan driver who had driven us there and was waiting and had heard the whole thing was as shocked as we were at the audacity of this woman. (And won’t be recommending anyone go there again). This is an absolute waste of time please avoid and don’t make the same mistake we did by going to this shambles of a factory.
title: Avoid, avoid, avoid. The worst experience and a waste of time and money.

body: We were supposed to go to Damro but went here instead as land slides had blocked the road.A very average factory tour: the attendant walked us through the entire tea-manufacturing process in their factory. Nothing spectacular, just an average tour. They didn't have a lot of varieties of tea for sale either.
title: An average factory tour

body: We live in USA and was visiting family in Sri Lanka. Our whole family took a tour of the factory. Then they served us tea, which tasted very good. We bought 5Kgs of tea from them, since they ensured that it would taste the same as the ones that they served. After we came back to USA, we tried the tea. All the tea tasted like rotten moldy grass with a hint of plastic. It was horrible. We are so disappointed that an actual tea factory sold us crappy, terrible tea.
title: Sold us rotten moldy grass tasting tea!!

body: Visit this place for a nice cup of tea and to buy tea leaves. Also they do factory tours where the kids can learn the routine and tasks of a tea factory.
title: A nice cup of tea

body: We were really disappointed with our visit to Pedro Tea Factory. Firstly when we arrived noone greeted us, the staff all ignored us and it was really unclear where we were supposed to go. We figured out we had to buy tickets and were then told to wait 10 minutes until the tour started. We waited 30 minutes without any further communication about the tour. Another staff member did give us a cup of tea but with no explanation, we weren't really sure if it was actually supposed to be for us. We chose a table to sit at, but they were all very dirty with bits of food and flies and dishes unclear from previous guests. Finally our tour guide came to get us for our tour, she was very unenthusiastic and came across as in a hurry and disinterested. During the tour, our guide was very rude to other guests in our group. The guide's accent was a bit hard to understand at the best of times (not her fault as English is her second language), but she told two members of our tour group (who English was also not their first language for) that taking photos was not allowed. They clearly did not hear her/understand what was being said, and instead of gently making sure they understood, she yelled at them "do you even speak English?!". After the tour was finished she just walked off without saying goodbye or thanks or anything. Such a bad experience from start to finish! The previous day we did a tour at Damro and it was amazing! I'd definitely recommend avoiding Pedro and going to Damro instead.
title: Really disappointing

body: Nuwara Eliya is a hill-station and we were not going to leave without seeing at least a couple of tea gardens and tea factories. Two of the most famous tea gardens in this town are the Pedro Tea Factory and Damro Labookellie Tea Factory.We drove to the Pedro Tea Factory. This is NOT a working factory and therefore we decided to skip the factory tour and instead walked part of the tea garden.
title: Damro factory is much better. If you are going to visit just one, go there. If you have time, can see both

body: The guide tried her best, but she is average and her explanations were very general and not insightful. The factory is in operation only at night hence the instruction given to us on the process was more or less in theory. The factory has a good view but still not worth the price you pay and the time spent.
title: Average

body: The tour we did was informative and reasonably priced. There was a very large group with no options for a smaller group. Overall glad we went but would maybe check out a different tea factory if we were to come again.
title: Informative tour

body: The factory tour itself cost 500LKR and for that you get to walk around the factory and see all the different machines and different stages of the tea making process. Our tour Gide spoke very good English and took the time to answer questions. The tour maybe lasted around 20-30mins. You can then sit in the cafe and taste one of the teas for free. There is also a gift shop. The views are really nice.
title: Value for money

body: Amazing tour , almost overwhelming with the gorgeous scenery and staff , the smell of the tea is stunning , the staff that work there are dedicated and passionate. Hard to believe that the traditional processes end up in our tea all round the world . The tasting process is an art passed through family’s . It also goes into our favourite Ahmad tea and helped us understand why it tastes so wonderful
title: Amazing amazing memories

body: this is apparently a working factory hence was expecting a lot from the tour. although the staff was friendly they seemed to be disinterested in conducting an informative tour. the shop has limited options in terms of packaging but was well priced. Yet to taste the tea!
title: tour was a let down

body: One of our highlights to tea country was our trip to Pedro tea factory. The tour was amazing. The process was explained and we saw the machines and every step of tea production our guide was lovely and guided us with expertise and passion I was particularly impressed how they included a man on our tour who had an impairment. They were considerate of his needs and he wasn’t left out. Tea tasting st the end was great and we purchased tea to take home. Highly recommend if you love tea.
title: Learning about tea production

body: This was one of the main reasons for our trip to Sri Lanka and this was such a disappointment. The tour when it got underway was taken by a lady guide who seemed so un-interested in her job and the customers were an inconvenience. It was so rushed and a large group whereby it was difficult to hear what was being said. This lady did not appear to want to be there and her body language exuded this. It was so rushed. Very very disappointing, don't waste your money, a small as the fee is, or more importantly your time you will be under whelmed
title: EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING

body: Everything about the visit was bad. Not sure if we got a particularly unmotivated guide, but she just repeated what she memorized and explained what each machine does. We asked several follow up questions, but her answer was not insightful. Also, we all get free tea but honestly the tea tasted worst than the cheapest tea I drink back home. They provide third grade tea. After drinking that tea, I definitely didn’t want to buy any tea from the factory. Lastly, now the tour fee is 250 lak. Overall, it was a waste of time. I could google and drink better tea at home.
title: Very disappointing

body: The tour was short and underwhelming. I came out with as little knowledge as I went in. Far nicer is the Hertance tea hotel.
title: Underwhelming.

body: Factory tour with the guide was very interesting and informative. They charge a nominal fee of LKR250 for adults and my kids were allowed without a charge. They run the factory during the night shift only so couldn't see most machines working but despite that one would get a good sense of how tea is produced.We also walk down the tea bushes but didn't see any plucking activity in that part unfortunately.I would recommend this place to people who have not been to a tea factory before.
title: Worth a visit

body: It is worth taking the time to do the tour: very informative and interesting! It only takes 30 minutes, and then you can their Tea.
title: Quick & interesting tour

body: Since this tea factory was very close to our Nuwara Eliya hotel, we decided to take a tour. It was a bit disorganized at the beginning, as we purchased our ticket and were then told to sit in a waiting area. Meanwhile, we saw people gathering and being handed aprons, and turns out this was our group, but no one told us. So we joined in and had an informative walk through the factory. Most of the work is done at night, as the tea picked during the day has to dry, so only a couple of machines were actually running. No problem, and they were nice enough to let us know this when we purchased the tour ticket.Our favorite part was the cup of tea provided at the end. We enjoyed sitting outside on the balcony with a lovely view of the plantation. We hope you enjoy the tour as much as we did!
title: Nice tour and delicious tea!

body: While the guide was fine, it wasn't a very rounded tour. They should start with showing tea plucking, through the factory with showcasing the old wood burners and letting people see the different grades. It should end with a tea tasting where ppl can try to taste the differences. Great location and definitely worth taking the walk to the waterfall as well.The guides (I overheard a few while we were there) should try to introduce themselves and give a little personal story of their relationship to the estate. I would assume our guide was the daughter of a estate worker who has learned english and is now guiding groups which is nice to see.
title: Not a rounded tour

body: We spent a couple of hours at the pedro tea factoryWe were guided by loshini who was very good at answering our questions and translated the information about how tea leaves were processed in english and Tamil as well. Highly recommended if you want an informative tour about tea leaves :)
title: Good informative tour!

body: This is a smaller, more historical tea factory, built in 1885. The entrance costs 250 rupee ($1.40) and the tour lasts about 20 minutes. The tour is very interesting and it includes a cup of tea. You can walk around the tea plantations afterwards. You'll see women working, they allow photos, but a small donation is expected.
title: Historical tea factory

body: Interesting tour which shows you from start to finish how tea is produced. The machinery wasn’t working the day we went but the tea tour was still worth it. Free cuppa at the end.
title: Interesting if you enjoy tea

body: Really worth the 20 minutes that the tour takes. Great to get an insight into how tea is produced as well
title: Interesting

body: It was a Sunday they were washing down the machinery and finishing production, fascinating. Like stepping back in time.
title: proper working lesson on tea making

body: This is a great place to go with kids.They have tea factory tour.u need to pay for that.But it’s worth for the cost and affordable.
title: Tea culture

body: Unfortunately our guide seemed really uninterested in showing us around and answering our questions. She did not even paid attention to us. Would not recommend!
title: Unfriendly Tourguide

body: Comparatively a small factory built in 1885, yet an interesting tour. Located just 3.5 km from the Nuwaraeliya city center makes its one of the few factories closer to the town. As soon as you enter the premises , it’s start smelling tea. Tickets for the tour is available at the counter in “Lover’s Leap” Ethical tea boutique. Boutique is located right opposite the car park down towards the tea estate. Tickets comes with a free cup of tea which is free to enjoy before or after the tour. Boutique's clean and well maintained ambiance was so relaxing and offer a perfect view of the greeny tea estate. There was a fair collection of Ceylon tea to be purchased. However, lesser verities. Didn’t see a large collection of flavoured or infused teas. Reason may be this place only sells the pure tea straight from their factory without any infusions or additions. Only pure tea as it is. “Lover’s Leap”, the Boutique got this name in reference to a nearby waterfall with the same name. Supposedly the name was given after an ancient prince and his lover leapt into death from the particular waterfall. Tour was fairly short since the factory is small (just about 10-15 minutes). But worth the experience. What I loved most is purchasing different kinds of Ceylon tea. If your itinerary is too tight and does not permits much time to travel a factory too far from city or long tea tour, this is an ideal place.
title: Ceylon Tea Tour

body: The tour took 15mins at most including the walk from the boutique to the factory and back. We were provided only very basic information about the manufacturing process,none about tea fields, tea bushes or plucking. We didn't have an opportunity to ask questions,as the guide simply told us (at what seemed like a random point of the tour) to take a seat in order enjoy a cup of tea, without saying goodbye or in any other way suggesting that the tour had come to an end. Expecting her to at least tell us what kind of tea we would be served (to this moment we do not know) or asking us whether we had any questions was apparently too much to ask. We would have at least partially understood this kind of attitude had the factory been busy,but we only came across three other guests in the facilities who had already been taken care of. Definitely not worth 250 rupees. We ended up finding out a lot more about tea production from blogs written by tourists who visited other factories,which I find very sad. Honestly I fail to understand the added value of taking the tour. You can simply stroll through the countless tea fields above the factory (with better views) and later enjoy a nice cup of tea at a restaurant while reading about tea production on wikipedia. I sure hope that the tours at other factories are more worthwhile.
title: A waste of time.

body: This factory is located in the middle of a beautiful tea estate. It feels weird when we are there. The tea factory, which was created by the British, is still running. If you are going to Nuwara Eliya, don't forget to visit this place.
title: One of old Tea Factory in Nuwara Eliya

Therefore we did not buy any presents here and considered the visit as a waste of time. Don't always believe youtubers :(

body: Not very special but it was fine. The view was very nice andthe free tea and a good price for the cake.

body: Interesting tour following the process from fresh tea leaves to tea packets.... with cuppa at the end. Great views. Not allowed photos in the factory. There were a lot of initiatives to look after their workforce.
title: Tour around eco friendly tea factory, not far from Nuwara Eliya

body: Pedro tea factory offers its visitors an interesting guided tour of the factory, giving valuable insight to all aspects of tea such as, steps of processing, types of tea, how it is being marketed etc. This factory belongs to a well established tea plantation group that supplies teas to many well known brands in the country, such as Dilmah.Guides speak good English and are professional and friendly. The tour takes only about 30 minutes. One must purchase an entry ticket which costs around Rs.250/= per person. *** Make sure to be there by 8.00 am in order to see the factory in full operation as they start their processing work very early in the morning.If you happen to go later in the day, you can still get a tour of the factory but you will not get to see as much, since the work is mostly done by mid morning and the workers get on with cleaning the machinery. Nevertheless, it would still be educational and worthwhile.At the end of your tour, you get to enjoy a complimentary cup of freshly brewed tea while enjoying the view of their beautifully maintained tea gardens. They also sell some fine teas, if you wish to purchase any. These teas are of very good quality, you'll not regret buying some.
title: Interesting Tour! High quality tea.

body: We really enjoyed our morning tour of the Pedro Tea Factory just out of Nuwara Eliya. We got to see all the stages of tea production and sample a lovely cuppa overlooking the plantation. A great way to spend an hour or so and very informative, especially if you're a tea drinker. It's got a special gentle vibe, tucked away in the hills.
title: Really interesting tour of the tea factory and walk in the grounds

body: We had a fascinating guided tour of the factory and learned all about the tea picking, withering and packing process. We then had a cup of tea and wandered through the plantation itself. Highly recommended.
title: Really fascinating tour

body: It starts off at about 8.15am, and involves a guided tour of the tea factory itself. This is not a massive tour group; each visiting group is taken on their own tour by a guide, even if the group consists of just 2 people! Literally no waiting time.The tour itself is very interesting, & he guide is knowledgeable and entertains questions asked by guests. After the tour, guests are allowed to roam the tea plantation by themselves! No one breathing down your back or watching your every move... Haha! Total freedom in a lovely tea estate.... finally, the tour ends with a warm cup of Sri Lankan tea. I thoroughly enjoyed this tour...!
title: Very well organized and enjoyable tour

body: If you’re a tea lover and have time to kill it’s a good place to go to. The tour was nice and the views were great. Very interesting.
title: Interesting tour with a great view

body: Went on tour of factory, could hardly understand the guide, nothing happening in the factory. Very little explanation of the picking process or tea varieties, offered a cup of tea at end of visit. I’m sure there are better places to visit.
title: Waste of time

body: Visited the Tea factory couple of days back, it was a wonderful experience. The staff is very polite and knowledgeable. They speak all three languages, property is in a beautiful location. it was indeed a very informative tour and the cup of tea at the end of the tour was a lovely touch.
title: Wonderful experience!

body: This is a very historical site in the tea industry. Pedro owns Lovers Leap. Unfortunately the lunch bell rang at 1pm and all the pickers in the plantation and people in the factory disappeared for 1 hour. There was no activity in the factory and the tour guide said they make the tea at night. She struggled to answer my questions and couldn’t say the difference between black tea and green tea. It would have been helpful to have an information sheet in English. There was no tea tasting either. Good view of the plantation though. Pickers willing to have photo taken if money given. I didn’t realise til after the visit about the historical importance of Pedro, that wasn’t mentioned either. They are marketing themselves as an eco centre also, but again not sure why? There is a huge woodshed out the back that seems to run the original equipment from the 1890’s.
title: Historical site but not much to see in fsctory

body: 20 mins away from Nuwara Eliya city center,we bought tea leaves,I think tea leaves are in good quality,don't know excellent,price is too reasonable,anyhow we enjoyed lot,
title: good tea factory

body: We had a quick tour and explanation of how tea is made - it was fine but quick. I was most disappointed with the selection of gifts - I didn’t end up buying anything because the selection wasn’t great. The grounds were beautiful though.
title: Lovely view

body: We arrived at the tea boutique just when a group started the factory tour. They told us the next tour would start in 20 minutes and asked us to take a walk around the tea plantation first. The view was truly amazing. After the walk, we went back to the tea boutique and waited. The group we saw earlier finished their tour and was given tea to drink. We continued to wait but nothing happened. Then a staff asked us if we wanted tea. We asked if the tour would start soon and was told that it would not start for another 15 minutes. We ended up waiting for around 40 minutes before the tour finally started. We were given aprons and shower caps to wear. The tour guide was soft-spoken and we could only hear part of the explanations. After the tour, we wanted to buy some tea to take home. There were many different types of teas and we had no idea about differences. When we asked the staff, she only gave us some half-hearted attention. It would have been better if they could put up signs next to the teas to explain the differences.

body: Potential not exploded. Could be amazing, stays on average. Good tea and views at the end. Nothing special. What a pity. The explanation is made while they dont have much going on. Hard to see it in action. Mainly cos they work at night. Hope to come back in the future and see it shining.

body: Very hospitable staff, breathtaking views whilst you away the tour sipping fresh tea. They even have a little shop where you can buy some tea

body: many varieties of tea and The tour was wonderful The guide was explained everything nicely also price is cheap

body: This tour gives a good insight to how tea is manufactured and is located in a very picturesque setting. The tour is not too long at 30 minutes and only costs R250 pp which we felt was reasonable.

body: The tour at the factory was kinda short but also cheap. And it was so nice to stroll on the tea plantations after the tour. Also cup of tea was offered.
title: Tea Factory

body: We got a fine tour through the factory. Be aware that they work during night, so most machines are turned off. Got a nice cup of tea after the tour. The tea they sell is quite overpriced so buy elsewhere.
title: Fine tour

body: A three wheeler from Nuwara Eliya centre to the Pedro costs 350-400 rupees. The estate is in a picturesque setting and the tour is very reasonably priced at 250 rupees per person. Pedro cares about its staff and the environment - both important factors when considering which plantation to visit. The workers were off and the cleaners were in when we went round, that was fine as they warned us. The best part was talking to the tea pluckers at the end. And the cup of orange pekoe!
title: Worth a visit if the tea pluckers are working

body: We arrived at Pedro Tea Factory via tuk tuk (we paid 500rupees from the city centre, negotiating it from an original 1000 rupee 'tourist rate') and were ushered to join a tour (250 rupees each for foreigners). What i couldn't really find information on, was if the tour timings were adhoc or at certain times in the day. When we arrived, everything seemed more adhoc - and it appears the tours run frequently enough and there aren't any minimum tour sizes for them to start (our tour group was 4, whereas others were 10+ people).... so arrive when you can and I'm sure the waiting time will be limited. Tour guide was friendly enough, communication was good and she was happy to take questions. You do get a free tea at the end of the tour and then we actually spent sometime just sitting and enjoying the view. There are plenty of tuk tuks waiting to take you home just outside of the gates or as many did to us on our walk down, offered to take us home.
title: Great place to learn a little and then enjoy the view

body: This was interesting if you’ve never been to a tea factory before, but on the day we visited the machines were not working which was a little disappointing. Also the guide who was very pleasant spoke in a quiet voice and was incomprehensible for most of the people in our group. Also we didn’t see the actual T plucking and all exactly how this was done which was disappointing and could’ve been explained in more detail. However the building and machinery was interesting to look at.
title: Ok experience.

body: We went to this factory because it has been awarded with multiple certificates for treating their worker ethically. They tour of the factory was only 250 rs. The tour is rather quick and the machines are not operating (they work at night) which for us was okay. It gave us a good enough idea about the production of the tea. Afterwards you get a tea and also can buy tea if you want to. I really liked to browse the little shop, since there was no hassle and nobody was pushing us to buy something. We could even try different teas and take our time to make a decision which tea we want in the end.
title: Ethical Tea Factory with excellent tea

body: All tea factories in Sri Lanka is same, we went to tea factory in Lipton seat, this one is also similar to that one, but the free tea they give after tour, is amazing ;) you have to pay 250 rupee per person...
title: The free tea they give is great

body: We think it is just another Tea Factory. I too thought the same. I have being to many tea factories in my life. But the Pedro tea factory itself is different. The building structure is unique and as explained by my Friend Nadun Madushan, the Assistant Manager, it is built in the style of an Chocolate Factory. In order to maintain a high standard of quality, tea manufacturing is done only during the night when the weather is colder. Therefore, the action is very low during the day time. But don't be worried there are plenty of staff who are well trained to take you on a guided tour on how tea is manufactured. Due to security reasons the management doesn't allow anyone to take photographs inside the premises. Their tea boutique is also a very cozy place to visit and have a nice cup of tea and purchase whatever the flavor you wish to have. And over looking the tea boutique is the lovely scenery of the tea estate. Time spent here is very relaxing and memorable. This place is a must visit to anyone who visits the beautiful Nuwaraeliya.
title: An experience that every tea lower should have

body: We went on a Sunday so no picking or processing happening but lovely staff showed us around .Certainly puts a different perspective on a simple cup of tea ! Such hard physical work for the ladies picking .Great tea samples after the tour.
title: Very interesting

body: Our group visited the Perdro Tea Plantation & factory as part of our tour of the Hill country. They produce Lovers Leap ethical tea.We were shown around the factory by a local plantation worker who explained the tea production process & showed us the various steps from picking to drying & quality control. She was very interesting in describing a very labour intensive process.We also saw tea pickers & had a cuppa in the factory tea shop. Very enjoyable & informative.
title: A Tea plantation visit is part of the Hill Country experience

body: The price of the tour is not much, but the commentary was pretty uninspiring. The only two sections of the factory working at the time was the sorting of the finished tea into its various grades from the top grade orange pekoe to the tea dust. We did see the first process but I didn't hear the name where the leaves are initially dumped in big bays to be dried with wood fire heat to remove enough moisture from the leaves to make them rubbery and then allow the rolling process. But there was no machine on to show the rolling, the fermentation, or the cutting etc. After seeing the sorting, we saw the packaged product ready for auction, then it was back to the shop for a cup of their tea but no explanation of what we were drinking etc. So a pretty short and basic tour of the factory with a commentary that hard to hear at the best of times, but was inaudible when the sorting machine was on. We didn't see any tea pickers. I think by the afternoon they were all clocking off.The tea fields were nice to look at. The tea in the cafe was nice.
title: Pretty uninspiring tour

body: We went to this on our way to Heritance Tea Factory. Unfortunately it was a Sunday so the factory wasn’t working but we saw a tea factory and got a good explanation of its working. Worth the hour stop. They don’t allow photos. No idea why not.
title: Worth a visit

body: Excellent tour followed by a lovely cup of Pekoe. No better place to find out what makes a good cuppa and - see photos- a bit of a looker!
title: A nice cup of tea

body: Interesting tour but two groups merged to one as they were short staffed so over 35 people walking around the factory together was not ideal. body: A good tea factory that can feel a good taste of tea with a very good view and also a place with nice waterfall view called Loverslip.
title: A factory very closer to town

body: Went here to have a look at the lounge .. it’s beautiful surrounded and overlooking the tea estate !! A cup of tea here just to sit and watch the view is great .. went venturing out in the tea estate itself plucking tea leaves !! The tea cake wasn’t the most delicious ones I’ve had but it was okie !!
title: Nice

body: Tea factory with factory tour and shop plus nice views. We had a brief group tour which cost 250LKR each for approx 30min tour. The tour guide was arguing with workers for a long period of time and I got the sense we were not welcome to watch the workers load up tea. That said we had a rudimentary tour of the factory and I left with more knowledge about tea than I came with. At the end we all had a complimentary cup of tea which was very nice and were encouraged to buy some tea at the shop. I think the tea here is better than other places but a bit disappointed by the tour.
title: Come for the tea, not the tour

body: The factory tour is extremely well presented and any questions from the visitors were well dealt with. Not to be missed if one has the opportunity to go
title: Well conducted tour

body: The visit was nice but a little bit short. We had a “free” tea cup at the end of the visit. The views are beautiful from the factory.
title: Nice

body: Entry to the factory is free. but if you want to enter inside the processing unit and see the different stages of tea leaves processing you will have to pay SLR 250 per head. The entire factory visit will take around 30 minutes time. You will be served complementary tea at the end of the factory visit. there are a lot of places around for clicks. Must visit place in Nuwra Eliya. Preferred time of visit morning till 12 noon.
title: How tea leaves processed for consumption

body: We went straight to the Tea Boutique and separately ask two staff members for a cup of tea. They each told us to sit and wait then disappeared. Waste of time.
title: Couldn't get a cup of tea!

body: Worth a visit and the guide answered all the questions although I do not know why photos were not allowed to be taken. No pressure was put on us to buy the tea.
title: Interesting process

body: The tea factory is an interesting place which provides a tour which is informative. There is a lot of talk about how little the tea pickers earn (~800lkr per day) which seemed like a ploy to get tips, which probably dont find their way to the tea pickers.
title: Quite Interesting, nice tea

body: Interesting tour round tea factory but the over-zealous guide was obsessed by telling us not to take photos! Accused one young lady of taking them when she hadn't. Must have though we were all competitor spies although there was hardly state-of-the-art innovative machinery to spy on!
title: Don't dare to take photos!

body: There were 2 options - 250 rupees for tea factory or 1000 for tea factory and tea picking. We opted for the latter and picked tea first. The lady took us down and we got dressed in the tea picking clothing, and she only said how to pick tea leaves and then left us to it for 20 mins. She didn’t explain anything about tea picking or the process. We then walked round the tea factory which wasn’t active with another uninspired lady who was on autopilot when explaining things. At the end we were given a lovely cup of tea but were not told anything about it. Visited another tea factory in our trip and had a much better experience and learnt so much from an enthisiastic guide who turned on the machine where the factory wasn’t active for us to help visualise the process, and then we bought tea from there!
title: Better tea factories

body: On arrival we were given the option of tea factory tour for Rs 250 or tea picking for Rs1000. We went for the latter which turned out to be a huge mistake. We were shown how to pick one tea leaf then left to our own divides for 20 minutes, whilst the guide was preoccupied with her phone. We were not told anything about the tea plantation or the tea picking process. After this we were taken on a tour of the factory, but all the machinery was off as they only use the factory at night. During the tour the guide was more interested with her friends, giggling and waving at them, than giving us any real information about the factory. She also spoke in autopilot and was inspiring. Overall a very disappointing visit and not worth the money. This trip was unforgettable for all the wrong reasons.
title: Disappointing visit - not worth the time or money

body: Disappointing tour of the tea factory as the guide had a poor English accent and spoke very quickly. Amazingly they did not sell the lovely green smocks which they insisted all visitors had to wear on the tour. BIG missed opportunity.
title: An Essential Part of a Sri Lankan trip - visit a tea factory, so we went to the Pedro Tea Factory.Guide spoke very quick

body: We visited a number of tea factories and got tired of the hard sell. Pedro tea factory was different. It had a lovely feel. The lady who showed us around was really lovely. There tea is delicious and there was no hard sell at all. Highly recommend
title: Excellent

body: I wasn’t really into this, but my lady was and the tuk tuk driver recommended it... you’ll take a 15 minute walk through the factory and see how tea is made... they let you have a tasting and hope you’ll buy something.
title: Not bad if you’re interested in seeing tea factory

body: Honestly we visited 2 tea factories and found this one the best . It was nice , the tour was really nicely done and the estates were soooo pretty and secluded. Totally worth the visit
title: Best tea factory in NE

body: We went out of our way to visit this tea factory due to a write up in the Lonely Planet. They did tours, but they were at a cost, and the factory is not in operation during the day, so there is not much to see. The tea room and gift shop was pretty uninspiring, so we spent about 5 minutes there and left. Waste of a tuk tuk fare.
title: No tours

body: We visited the factory in January 2019. De tour guide was very hard to understand because of her poor English. We didn’t understand a thing.. After the short tour, we got a cup of tea (which was included the tour price of 200rp). The waiter also offered us a fruit cake. We asked if it was including the price and he answered yes. We got a old Christmas cake... when we wanted to leave he told us to pay 450rp for the cake. We complained about it at the cashier but all we’ve got a was a sorry and he couldn’t speak English reason. We didn’t get our money back and left the factory with a unsatisfied feeling.
title: Don’t accept the ‘free’ cake and avoid this factory

body: The cafe and the views and setting are the highlight of this trip. The tour with a very uninterested guide and the hard sell afterwards put a dampener on the visit. The tour is free though and you tip as you see fit.
title: Lovely tea and cake but disappointing tour

body: The tour was very efficient, but felt somewhat rushed and that the guide was pretty much just quoting a memorised spiel. The free cup of tea on the verandah afterwards was ordinary, but appreciated, and it does have a good view of the tea plantations. It was interesting to see the factory, but if you can plan to be there after 11am you've got a much better chance of seeing the tea coming in and being sorted. We were a bit early so the first load of the day hadn't yet arrived.
title: Very efficient

body: It's easy to join a group to take a tour of this factory. The tour runs really fast, and assumes you already know something about tea and how it is produced. After the tour is over they serve you a cup of tea produced in the area.
title: fast tour

body: We visited this factory on a Monday and there was no tea production happening so we were taken around the machinery which was not very interesting. Our tour guide spoke on auto pilot and was more interested in waving to her co-workers than in explaining anything to us. We were provided with a cup of tea afterwards but there was no explanation of what tea it was. At RP250 it is not expensive but it’s really not worth the time.
title: Not worth the visit

body: During our sri lanka trip we also wanted to visit a tea factory and since our accomodation in nuwara eliya was close to the san pedro facility we went there for a tour around noon. The entrance fee has meanwhile increased to 250 rupees which is still not very high, but the whole tour took also only around 20 minutes and was not very informative. At noon there was no production in the factory that day, however with production in the background we would have probably not understood our tour guide. We got a cup of tea afterwards but also without any further comments or explanation. Seems the quality of the tours in this factory has quite a wide variation.
title: 20 min tour...

body: Nice visit to small central located tea factory , in town of nuwara eliya , it was very Informatative , didn’t take hours and you got to see the working of how tea is made and processed . Very enjoyable
title: Great little tour

body: We bought almost all the tea from the shop and it’s really tasted! the explanation of how they make the tea is really curious
title: Nice!

body: We enjoy drinking tea and had never experienced what goes into growing and processing tea until we visited the Pedro Estate Nuwaraeliya tea factory. Enjoyable day out in very scenic part of Sri Lanka. Very clean and tidy facilities and great cup of tea. About 20 minute drive from city centre. Great drive. Our tour guide Sivakavj at the Banquet Boutique was the perfect guide with excellent knowledge and very friendly customer support. Ask for her personally and you will not be disappointed.
title: Tea at its best

body: I've visited many tea plantations in India and Sri Lanka. The tour here was very good and everything well explained. The guide didn't take us into the plantations or explain about Silver tips, white and green tea. Also, the tea offered after the tour is nice but the Damro tea factory is much better for a relaxing tea (free) and cake (paid) overlooking the plantations. Blue Field is also good to visit.
title: Average

body: The marketing for this factory is amazing, though note you are not allowed to take any pictures during the tour and have to wait until the guides are done with their lunch which can be any time after 2 pm. Tea sampling consists of 1 tea only, which is questionable given that you pay for your tour. Visit another tea factory instead.
title: Slightly hyped up tea factory

body: Really enjoyed the short visit here. The tour guide was really good, knew her stuff and very friendly to chat to. Visited on Christmas Day when the processing wasn’t happening so can’t comment on what it would be like on a working day.
title: Very nice, the tour was good

body: Me and my family really enjoyed visit in Pedro tea factory.It was very informative and kids liked getting to know how tea is made.Tea tasting was enjoyable and it's free of charge.The landscaped are breathtaking.You can just walk freely among tea plantations and enjoy the atmosphere of this beautiful place.The prices of tea were very reasonable in comparison to other places that we visited later.
title: Nice visit

body: Lovely tea factory with interesting tour which takes place every 10 minutes. Lovely outdoor area to have a cup of tea afterwards.
title: Cosy tea factory with good tour

body: Paid 250rupees for the tour.. it took about 20min all together.. the lady spoke very fast and rushed the whole process... She also asked whether she could give my change later however she didn't and I forgot about it so I don't know if she does that to everyone for side note to anyone reading this. We got some tea at the end and we didn't even know what kind of tea we we were drinking... The factory was cool inside and that's about it... I guess it's a must do for something to do in Nuwara Eliya. We took a stroll around the tea plantation which was nice and had some sick views of the dam and Mountains.
title: Fastest tour i got

body: Visited Pedro Tea Factory staff is simply amazing and well explained the process step by steps. Entry fee for factory visit is LKR 100 for locals and LKR 250 for foreigners. You can taste the tea and sales outlet is there to purchase tea. Good is thing is, lover's waterfall is around the factory. Amazing experience
title: Amazing experience

body: Great guide who explained everything clearly and concisely. Sixpacks of tea seem expensive at 2000 rupees but each pack of tea is 125g for just under £1.50 so good value really for a class product. Teaworkers were striking in Nuwara Eliya while we were there. They want 1000 rupees a day instead of the current 850. I so hope they get it as it is such a hard life.
title: Lovely setting for a very interesting visit.

body: Visited the tea factory and guided by the volunteer, about how the tea processing takes place ,step by step. Took about 25 minutes to finish the session. Then we were all served, crystal clear golden tea, aromatic and refreshing. Bought some tea packs also.
title: Factory visit

body: Chose the Pedro tea factory if you are wanting an authentic experience. Only 200 rupee per person for a guided tour with tea sample at the end.
title: Traditional tea factory experience

body: Average place to see tea garden, little bit of history of tea industry in Sri Lankan hill country. You could walk down the tea bushes. You can buy tea and refresh yourself with a nice and warm cup of tea.
title: Off for tea

body: nice loving scenery and the weather was really good. the factory is very traditional as they are still using very basic machinery and process to product tea
title: love the scenery

body: Another tea estate with lush green tea gardens. Enjoy the tea testing session and feel the aroma of it
title: Tea estate

body: A nice tea factory where they make primarily black tea. Staff is nice which takes you through the factory and explain the process.
title: Tea factory

body: Having read mixed reviews we were pleasantly surprised with our visit. Well signposted, easy booking, 250LKR pp, lovely guide, interesting tour and great cup of tea. Good value for money.
title: Tearrific!!

body: A charming tea factory. We did a factory tour followed by a cup of tea then we were able to wander through the nearby slopes watching the women pick tea. The factory was very interesting and so clean.
title: A charming visit

body: I’ve been at Pedro Tea Factory to times and it was very interesting both times. It was a friendly guide, who showed us that old and very traditional factory. After the tour you will be invited for a nice cup of tea. Also you can buy tea with a high quality for a reasonable price.
title: Nice Place to Visit

body: Pedro Tea Factory is not quite as fancy as others in the area but definitely worth a visit. The staff was friendly and helpful. There is a outside area where you can have a cup of tea and enjoy the beautiful view.
title: Nice staff and tea room

body: A good tour, although rather quick (roughly 20-30 mins). We came on a Sunday so only one machine was working, and no tea picking - not to mention torrential rains. Our tour guide was really informative, giving us plenty of info although it would’ve been nice to hear about more about the founding of the estate and the fermentation process. But for 250lkr and a great cup of tea at the end (which we then purchased for a great price) it’s definitely worth the trip from Nuwara Eliya. The views are beautiful and I’m sure during the week when the pickers are out and the weather is more pleasant a stroll around the fields would be worth it. I’d recommend getting a list of questions you want to ask, as they’re happy to answer any questions if you find you haven’t had one answered.
title: Quick tour, full of information and a great cup of tea.

body: Situated proudly as the tea factory at the highest elevation within Sri Lanka the factory produces some of the best tea in the world. A tour can be organised on arrival to see the process. A tea shop also allows you to taste and buy some tea.
title: You will love tea after you visit

body: You’re shown around the processing factory. The tour finishes off in the tea shop where you can then stroll around plantation. We’re big tea drinkers so we enjoyed it. We even chatted with some of the tea ladies in the fields. Fun fact: their collection bags are attached to their hats (not their backs)
title: Informative tour of tea production in the home of tea

body: We took this tour and another on the same day, this tour was educational and we learnt a lot about the tea making process which is good however there was no option to walk around the plantation after the tour, it seemed as though it was more effort and nobody came to show us the gift shop either which was strange. The tour cost 250LKR pp. It was a rather hurried trip and we only stayed for around 30 mins from arrival time to leaving. Other plantations offer a more relaxed welcome.
title: Good tour but not much happening

body: We visited this factory on 4th October and were looking forward to a tour around their site. Unfortunately we didn’t make it to this point. After buying our ticket for the tour we spent almost 40 minutes sat waiting for it to start, after being told it was a 10 minute wait. After around 30 mins we were told it would be another 5 minutes and waited another 10 before leaving. It was very disappointing to see that they had chosen to prioritise the bus tours over our custom. It also did not help that the waiting area was completely infested with flies. We were given a cup of tea to try whilst we waited, with one of the cups arriving with the previous users lipstick on which is always very appetising. The tea was weak and not particularly enjoyable.All of this mounted together helped our decision to leave without the tour starting. We would recommend there are plenty of other tea factories in the Nuwara Eliya area where they treat all customers with respect.
title: Poor service, poor tea

body: This place is close to Nuwara Eliya. It’s a 40 min walk or a quick Auto-rickshaw. Our guy took us there from town, waited for us and took us back to the hotel for 600 rupees. We did a tour which was as only 20 min and really quite interesting. It was 250 rupees each and the woman taking the tour was quite engaging and interesting. Nice cuppa tea at the end. An easy and relatively quick way to see a good tea plantation.
title: Interesting easy tour

body: This very old original tea estate offers tours to visitors of the main factory during the day as the tea is actually made at night when it is cooler. Clear explanations of the various levels of tea and a beautiful cup of tea at the end. Stunning location close to town.
title: A tour of the actual factory is comprehensive and interesting

body: Well worth a visit, very informative and interesting.All staff were friendly and no sales pitch at the end too
title: Interesting and great setting

body: once completed tour go to the tea house to enjoy a full flavoured tea. staff friendly and helpful. You can purchase tea there.
title: Interesting tour of tea factory

body: To be fair, it was interesting and was set in stunning Countryside. We learned about the tea making process and that was an enjoyable experience - but because they make ‘light’ tea most of the really interesting work and processing is done overnight, meaning the tour was primarily around an empty and quiet factory - more like a museum tour, which is not what it was billed as. Worth it ifyou have time to kill and are in the area, but would not go out of your way. Plus, as always, the shop is very overpriced.
title: Interesting But Not That Great

body: probably best to see during the wek we went on a saturday and nothing workingguide was pleasant and tea afterwards refreshingno hard sell which was nice as well
title: interesting

body: Visited Pedro having been left wanting on a trip to Stone Gate the previous day. Pedro is actually based on the plantation and you can see the tea plants and pickers in action. Good tour and explanation, but machines aren’t working as the quality of tea they produce is made at night (when cooler to slow down the the fermentation process) and I guess it would be dangerous anyway to walk around a factory in production anyway. Nice cup of tea afterwards, and a very soft sell in the shop, with really good prices. Afterwards had a wander through the tea plants and then walked up to Lovers Leap. Well worth a visit.
title: Good tea factory experience.

body: One of the reasons we went to Sri Lanka was to see a tea factory in production. Owing to the type of tea they produce here the production only takes place at night. We were given a quick tour around looking at inactive machines which made us none the wiser. You are then left in the reception area to watch a marketing video about how wonderful Pedro is and how they are helping the community etc (and given a cup of tea!). Given the lack of tea production you see on this waste of time tour, it would be far more useful to show a video of the tea production, at least then you would not feel you were leaving as badly informed as you were when you arrived! There are tea factories where you can see tea being produced and I suggest you visit one of those!!
title: Waste of Time !!

body: Interesting place to visit. We came at about 8:30 AM (visiting hours are 8:00-11:00 AM and also in the afternoon, but I can’t remember exact hours). We immediately got a guide (entrance fee - 250 rupees per person, but guide is for free, you can leave tips, if you want). The guide was kind and told us everything about the factory clearly and we went through all the steps: from picking leaves to packing a tea. In the end of the tour we could taste a cup of their tea while enjoying the tea fields view from the big windows. You can buy some tea in their shop and have a walk trough tea fields, even talk with the workers. Really nice time we had! It took us ~ 1 hour.
title: Worth a visit!

body: We were only staying about 3 mins down the road from this factory so it was the natural place to visit. Maybe not as grand or as big as some of the other factories, but our experience was excellent. Some days the factory is not in full production and this is due to the weather. When it is full and raining the tea leafs are not growing and therefore are not being picked.It was in half operation when we were there, and the lady who escorted us around for almost an hour was excellent. She advised she was the daughter of parents who had also worked at this factory for many years. She had been there for more than 8 years working also, and had climbed the ladder to a tour guide supervisor.There is a 250lkr entry fee and that covers the tour and a cup of tea at the end. The lady clearly explained in very good English the full process while taking us through the different drying, rolling, and sorting rooms of the factory. She welcomed our many questions.A worker at the factory or in the field does an 8 hour shift and gets paid 850lkrs for that shift. All workers at this factory live in company provided housing, so while the pay is very low in comparison to most western countries, the workers we spoke to are very happy to have steady work and a roof over their heads. So a great thank you to the senior tour guide at Pedro, well done! We are far more educated now.
title: What a great way to learn about tea

body: When we visited the Pedro Tea Factory the weather was too wet for tea picking so the factory was not operational. Nonetheless we had an excellent guide and it was fascinating to see the equipment and learn about all the different teas and how they process the tea leaves
title: Very Interesting Tour

body: Interesting to see the factory and get a better understanding of all the process steps for making tea. Unfortunately the factory is running during nighttime, so you do not get to see the process in working, but you get to see all the Machines and get an explenation of all the steps. The tour is finished by getting to try a cup of the from the factory, and you can buy a lot of differnet tea sorts as a souvernier
title: Visit the factory and enjoy a cup of tea with a great view

body: We visit Pedro tea factory in August 2018. It is only 10 minutes to Nuwara Eliya the factory is working only nights. They made a quick tea factory tour and served a cup of tea at the end of the tour. They are selling also their own tea. You are paying 250 rupies ( less than 2usd) for person. You may find another place which is free on the way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya.
title: Tea factory vis

body: Visited early in the morning as an alternative activity to our trip to Horton Plains being cancelled. They were extremely helpful, despite the electricity being off, they managed to make us a hot and welcome cup of tea and a tour of the factory. The tour is free and there is a small shop to purchase the estate Tea from. It is useful to offer the factory guide a small tip of 100/200 rupees.The factory is full of the most original machinery much of which is still in operation today, so if you are a lover of this sort of thing, you would definitely enjoy a visit.I was surprised at how quickly tea leaves are turned into tea, within 24 hours and that the aluminium lined bags they pack the tea into at the end of the process can keep the tea for upto 2 years.The estate announces that it is an ethical company with some opportunity for the workers to be involved and would appear to offer more medical care and education than some others do.I wasn't sure about this place as there were some remarks about the speed of the tour and the guides accent, but we did not feel rushed at all and the guide was clear, helpful and very friendly.
title: Interesting and helpful guide

body: Went round as a small group, unfortunately due to the rain the factory wasn't operating so we couldn't see it in action. However it was good to see and learn about the process & machinery, the guide though wasn't able to tell us anything about the history and was unable to answer a lot of questions.
title: Interesting but could have been more informative

body: Our guide was a very poor “English” speaking lady. The tour was very fast. You do not visit the tea plantation itself, only the factory. Afterwards you might get a cup of tea.
title: Little bit disappointed

body: We went into the visit without expecting much; there were mixed reviews so we just hoped it would either be good or funny if it was a total failure. After paying for our tour (250LKR per person) we had to wait for a guide to arrive, although this only took a few minutes. After the guide arrived we went into the factory. It was pretty... empty. It also seemed like the woman who gave us the tour was sick and tired of her job because she zoomed through the factory like a Formula 1 car with rockets strapped on the back. I also think it will be pretty hard for most non-native English speakers to understand what the guide is saying. The whole tour wasn't very convincing, nothing was working and there wasn't much of an impression to be gained from the tour. Moreover, the tour seemed kind of fake, after we noticed the "bags with tea" in the storage room had a text on them saying they were from March 2018. TL;DR - It was a short but decently fun tour, just don't go in with too many expectations because you will most likely be disappointed.
title: Zoof zoof through the factory

body: Actually got the chance to go amongst the tea bushes and pick tea leaves if you.
