I believe not many tea factories allow you to do this but this one does and it is near the town of nuwara eliya so it is very convenient if you’re staying around town. Didnt go for the tour though as we went for another tour at another factory previously and i dont see how the process would be much different.
title: Tea leaf picking

body: We went for a tour to this factory. Our guide was a lady that spoke very unclear english. She guided us at a high speed through the production facility where nobody was working. Only during the night there is production. So after the tour we have seen all the machines but still do not know exactly how the production is being done.Afterwards you receive a cup of tea.
title: A little bit disappointing

body: This is an excellent Tea factory experience. The guide Kalai vani was excellent. The view is beautiful. Tea very good. A good experience.
title: TEA FACTORY

body: Having spent time at other tea factories in Sri Lanka, we hadn't planned to visit but a miscommunication with our tuk-tuk driver brought us here en route to another activity; we weren't blown away by it and felt that the other factories we visited offer a better experience. We came on a non-production day and joined a tour with one other couple; it was delivered very quickly with very little enthusiasm and was not as interesting or informative as those in other factories we visited. At the end, we were given a cup of tea with no information as to what type of tea it was: more background and details would've been appreciated, or even a tasting of different types of tea. The views around the factory were amazing and it was fascinating to see the estates.
title: Disappointing experience

body: We went here for the tour and tea picking experience. Tour was very informative but you weren’t allowed to take photos. I was impressed some of the machines were installed in 1950s- built to last in those days! Tea from here is wholesale sold on to big companies who blend it to their own specifications. There were 65kg bags in the packing area!At the end you get a cup of tea to try.Being a photographer I really wanted to get some photos of the tea pickers but it seemed they weren’t working the Monday we went. We managed to see some further out of town so got some pictures then. Worth a visit!
title: Interesting tour

body: We had a short but informative tour of the factory in a small group and learnt heaps about tea making. This dispelled some of the mystery and myth. Highly recommend to anyone with an hour to spare
title: Factory tour

body: We enjoyed a very interesting and informative tour of the tea plantation at the Lovers Leap Pedro Tea Factory.The tour is quite short and takes you through the factory, explaining the various stages in tea production from harvest to drying, to grading and to packaging. The guide spoke English and was very well informed about the process and the history of the plant.Afterwards you are given compkimentary delicious tea on the balcony overlooking the plantation where there are lovely views and you are able to go for a walk down among the tea plants which was something we really enjoyed.They have a small shop selling their tea if you want to buy presents, absolutely no hassle or pressure though. A great morning or afternoon out; highly recommended.
title: Excellent Tour

body: Nice to do, good quality tea and friendly staff.The guide and the toor was a bit short, very little explanation and not deep.Quality of the factory is good, as well as the accommodation around, but a good guiding with quality explanation would be a big benefit.No Comercial pushing, that is something to appreciate!You can walk in the tea plantation alone, that is nice, but if a guide would explain a bit it would be nicer.A must do if you are there.Not recommend with a wheelchair or baby equipment.
title: Round trip Sri Lanka

body: If you’re a tea lover and are hoping for a magical tea experience in Sri Lanka, I wouldn’t recommend here. We found the tour pretty dull - not very informative or given with any excitement. When we arrived, the reception and shop were dark with no lights turned on which wasn’t very welcoming but also made it hard to look around the shop. The tour was very quick and lacked energy. No production which is ok but would be nice to turn on a couple of machines briefly to see how they work. Got back to the visitors area and waited a while for a cup of tea and when we got the tea, no description was given so we had no idea what type of tea it was. Put us off buying anything as by the end we still didn’t really know how it was made or what it was. If you’re travelling on to Ella, the Halpe tea factory there is fantastic and will give you a hands on tea experience with a long and informative tour. Would recommend hanging on till there :)
title: Underwhelming

body: The tickets said price 200R and were sold to us at the factory for 250R! Unprofessional! The tour of the factory took not even 10 minutes and felt very rushed.
title: Not worth it.

body: We learnt more from our guide before we got to this place. It was interesting but missing parts of information regarding the growing of tea. It would have been more interesting if the factory was actually working the afternoon we visited. We were told they only function at night due to the correct temperature for processing tea.
title: Interesting but lacking

body: Good educational tour but go early to avoid the heat in the afternoon. Pamper yourself to a cup of good tea at their cafe and then to shopping at their souvenir shop.
title: Educational tour and rest stops

body: They took us Factory Tour and explain Tea producing procedure A - Z. Offered nice cup of Tea. You can buy fresh Tea as well.
title: Learn about Tea manufacturing

body: Fab your of a wonderful tea factory , so interesting and great selection of teas to buy ( and drink after tour ) beautiful location with fabulous grounds to amble round. Staff were lovely too , thank you
title: Great experience

body: Did the detailed survey of tea factory . where we wereexplained of how the different kinds of tea powders are made
title: Tea Factory

body: Well worth a visit as it provides a great insight into the tea making process through the guided tour.This was followed by some tea sampling.Pedro is an ethical tea producer so well worth a visit.
title: Great insight into the tea making process

body: While in NE for a workshop, we went over to Pedro Tea Factory to buy some tea. Wow....the place itself was amazing...clean, neatly laid out garden....wonderful tea centre and the best part - 2 amazing sales women ....most probably from the surrounding plantations. They were so knowledgeable on the tea they were selling ..... As part of the Ethical Tea partnership i think the Pedro Tea Factory is doing a great job ...its just 2 kms from the city centre on the Kandapola Road....A must visit
title: The best place to buy Tea in Nuwara Eliya

body: We really enjoyed the tour of this working factory. We did not appreciate the hard manual work required for tea picking and sorting thereafter. We have all resolved that we MUST pay more for our tea as the tea pickers don’t get paid enough- it seems less than US$10 per day. Shocking!
title: Great tour of a working tea factory

body: You have to pay for the tour but it is cheap and you get a free cup of tea. Was nice and informative/Interesting. The nicest thing was to walk around the tea plantation before/after...very pretty and great views.From here you can walk up to the lovers leap waterfall which is a lovely walk.
title: Tea Factory tour

body: I did a number of tours of the tea plantations and tea factories while in Sri Lanka. This was the only one which I had to pay for (though only 200 rupees - about USD $1.25). However it was the most perfunctory. We got the factory tour in a large group (after waiting for others to slowly stop in and accumulate) and one cup of tea at the end. There was a small shop with a limited selection of teas to buy after the tour. On the plus side it has easy access from the closest town Nuwara Eliya and was right in the tea fields. Of the tea factories I visited this had the best access to the tea fields for spectacular views and the opportunity to take close up photos of the lady tea pickers. For that alone it is worth visiting - with your camera or iphone in hand.
title: Decent Tour: the closeness to the tea fields makes it

body: I’ve been to several tea factories in Sri Lanka and Pedro is nice as you get to see a working factory. Sadly on the day we went it was not operating due to a public holiday but nevertheless you get to see inside it and you can tell that it’s not just a display factory like many others I’ve been to. The tour was only 200rps and included a cup of tea at the end (which wasn’t great). I wouldn’t buy tea here but if you’re into your tea and want to see a functioning factory it’s worth a visit.
title: Working factory experience!

body: We were taken to this plantation and factory by our driver as part of a planned itinery. The tour of the plant was very informative and the guide spoke extremely well. We left very informed, just unfortunate that we didnt see the factory in action (works at night), and couldnt take photos in the factory. Got to taste some tea (without milk as its not the done way), and walk amongst the plantation. We left satisfied that we had been to what we wanted to see and hear, but feel there could have been more. Sadly didnt see anyone picking leaves, but that was just where we were at the time. All family happy.
title: Left satisfied but wanting more

body: We were looking forward to seeing a working tea factory in action, learn about tea and enjoy a tasting to understand different varieties and qualities of tea. None of this actually happened as we were shown around an empty tea factory looking at machines and being told the absolute minimum by a bored and annoyed guide. After the tour we were given a cup of tea and encouraged to buy tea from the shop. Far too commercialise. If you want to learn about tea and enjoy a tea tasting go somewhere else, this was totally not worth the time or energy.
title: Guided tour of empty factory and no tea tasting

body: Was heading for the Lover’s Leap, when I found this tea factory, and thought I’d buy some to bring back home. Tried to ask if it was organic, the women in the tea saloon didn’t understand, so after getting a hold on the manager, I sort ofGot an answer: they are “sort of organic” he said - using some chemicals. They do seem to have great focus on social responsibility, like houses for all their workers, which is great. Their lightest tea was the best, in my opinion, but also the BOP.
title: Nice tea factory taking social responsibility

body: The tour was quite short, but for those who don't know much about how tea is made, the tour is quite informative. The tour costs Rs.200/= which is very reasonable. The young guide who gave the tour was very pleasant and also answered most of the questions. The tour ended with a tasty cup of tea. You can also buy tea from there for about Rs.500/=, but I hear that there are more popular places in Nuwara Eliya that sell better quality tea (a couple of hundred rupees more expensive though!). We definitely came out knowing more about different types of tea. Not sure if the staff noticed, but we enjoyed the tea with the snacks we had brought. We also had our packed lunches outside the tea boutique area overlooking lush green tea plantations.There were bathrooms at the tea boutique and both men/women's bathroom were fairly clean.Overall, it was a great experience.
title: A Reasonably Priced Tea Tour

body: I came quite late there so the factory was nearly closed but the stuff was so nice to give me a tour - it’s quite short but interesting. Then you can have a cup of free tea witch is phenomenal!!! Very good experience at Pedro Tea Factory!!!
title: Good experience !!!

body: Pedro tea factory is situated closer to Nuwaraeliya city limits. You can take a tuk-tuk from the town or bus which travels on udupussellawa road. You'll get a brief while moving on a factory visit about the tea making process where you can clarify yourself and finally you can enjoy a hot cup of Ceylon tea as well. :)
title: If you're a tea enthusiastic, yes....!! It'll be worth:)

body: It was unfortunate for me as I visited the Pedro Tea Plantation on Good Friday. There is still a factory tour but there was no production and we are only shown all the machines without the tea leaves.If you plan to explore the tea plantation, you might want to wear long pants. To get a nice shot in the middle of the tea plantation, you have to walk in between the super narrow path.
title: Good experience to see a Tea Plantation

body: Had just complete the journey on the tea train so where better to go than visit a tea factory. As we had just stayed for two nights at a tea plantation we only really wanted to visit factory. We were taken round a by lovely lady (Sivakavi Kalaivani) who spoke amazing English with an occasional word with a Scots accent - lovely to hear. Not all the machinery was working as it was late in the afternoon but that did not spoil the experience. Commencing with the drying areas for the tea all the way down to packed product. When finished we adjourned to Lovers Leap (tearoom) where we tasted several varieties of tea - really delicious. We had taken with us a iced fruitcake from the UK so what better way to finish the afternoon with Ceylon tea and English cake. Well worth the visit.
title: Lovely visit around a genuine tea factory

body: Visited with my dad, and we had a lovely walk down to the tea plantains were we could see the ladies busy at work.They were doing guided tours of the factory for a small price but as the machines were not working we did not join in. We did sit in the cafe and enjoy a lovely cup of tea.Found the service to be a little slow- but pleasant all the same.
title: Lovely Plantation

body: We were staying overnight in Nuwara Eliya and borrowed bikes to visit the Pedro tea factory. The ride up the hillside was tough but it was so beautiful to cycle the paths through the plantation we didn't mind. The tour itself lasts about 30 minutes and the smell of the fresh tea is intoxicating in the drying room. Our guide spoke perfect English and was happy to answer questions. After the tour we tasted some of the tea, which was delicious! Definitely worth a visit if you have a free morning.
title: Stunning location and interesting tour

body: Its a small factory and when i visited, it was not operational. They showed us around and offered us a cup of tea at the end. Costed 200. It was OK trip and only thing working for it was that this was the closest factory to the city. Many people come by tuk tuk (400-500 Rs) but one can easily find bus from city center which drops you just outside the factory and cost you like 20 rs. The path leading to lovers leap is just opposite to factory (passing through tea plantation of pedro estate) and both activities can be coupled together.
title: Closest Factory to Town

body: Wasn’t a high cost for this tour and you get to have a roam afterwards. Our tour guide doesn’t seem to get that much enjoyment from the job and it felt a little underwhelming but it was still informative and I learnt stuff about tea- which was the point. It’s good to combine with a loop walk up to lovers leap and then get a tuk tuk back to town
title: Interesting little tour

body: I had already visited two tea factories so i did not bother taking the tour, but i rested in the cafe where i watched a documentary about Pedro Tea Estate and then enjoyed a free cup of tea. However there were quite a few people taking the tour and they seemed satisfied. I hiked here after passing by Lover'sLeap waterfall, but the last kilometer is along a busy road which was not too enjoyable.
title: Nice place to enjoy a cup of tea

body: A tuk tuk from town should cost about 500 each way.This is a nice tea factory. It's interesting to look around how it all works.
title: A nice hour spent looking at tea plantation

body: We travelled from Kandy to Pedro tea plantation by train which took us about 4 hours which was great. When we arrived at the tea plantation we were given a cup of tea and a tour of the factory which was rushed and took us twenty minutes. A total waste of time and a waste of my holiday. I was excited that I booked this tour prior to my holiday and I feel totally let down
title: Disappointing

body: This was not a very exciting venture. However it was interesting to know that the tea made here is sold and repackaged by big brands. It was also educational to see the process of tea making. Also the views at the location were great.
title: Educational tour

body: We dint know this and ended up just taking a stroll at the tea gardens. You can also buy the tea at the factory.
title: Closed on Sundays

body: The people try to force you to do the tour. The place is small and not as beautiful as other tea locations such as Talawakelle Tea Estate and Edinburgh Tea Estate. I would personally avoid and go to the above.
title: Small and forceful

body: Went there by Tuk-tuk, paid 200 rp per person for a guided tour around and a cup of tea afterwards. The tour takes no longer than 20 minutes and gives you the basic information about the tea making process. Smaller place compared to the big tea factory’s in the area. I would guess also less tourists. Which we love. After the tour we walked into the plantation and talk to the working ladies. A nice anc cheap experience.
title: Beautiful location

body: Our guide was friendly and the factory interesting. It did feel like we learnt the rudiments of the process and given we only had a limited time, this worked for us. If you want a more in depth bus-to-cup tour, you'll have to look elsewhere.
title: OK

body: I have visited the Pedro factory twice now, once with my partner and a second time with my Mum. It is very reasonably priced at just 200rs for a 20-30 minute guided tour and cup of tea.Our guide Kalaivane was superb! Friendly, informative and the daughter of a tea picker so able to gave a very personal and honest account of the tea industry. An enlightening experience I would definitely recommend!
title: Enlightening experience

body: Visited this factory... they give you a tour inside the factory where you can see how tea is made and you can enjoy different types of tasty teas.
title: Cool Experience!

body: Lovely, quaint, old tea factory. Tour was very informative and views were fantastic. Tea quite expensive.
title: Traditional tea factory

body: This is essential if one is to understand Tea in Sri Lanka. Excellent tour of a working factory with nothing missing. The real facts.
title: How it all works.

body: I visited with my friends and family from Norway,Serbia,China, Cambodia and Vietnam. It's very beautiful place with different varieties of tea. They explain about use and benefits of different types of tea.
title: Great experience

body: The visit is very very quick, the speaker speaks fast, and is not understandable, even by British tourists who were with us!!! (We are French). You also cannot take any pictures! Then you go for tasting the tea. They offer just one type of tea, and we had to ask several times to have more even if we pay for it!!! They are not caring at all. I do not recommend this place. There are plenty of tea factories offering visit for free and that like to share their knowledge and passion. Go definitely there and not at Pedro. We should ask lonely planet team to remove it from their next book edition!
title: Very poor service and useless visit

body: Good tour with a guide explaining the processes. Interesting to see how old the machinery was and still working. Strangely no photography allowed.Nice views outside of the reception area but not impressed with shop.
title: Interesting - worth a visit

body: This was our first of two tours of tea factories. It was inexpensive (about $2US) and well organized with an attractive display area and I would recommend it if you have a mild interest in the tea making process. However, we were hoping for a longer, more in-depth tour but our guide was hard to understand and her lack of English meant that she was unable to answer questions so we left a little disappointed.
title: A well-organized tour of a factory in an attractive estate

body: We came here in the afternoon of our day trip to Nuwara Eliya after riding the scenic train. Blue Lanka, our tour agency, recommended it so we thought we would give it a try. The factory is wonderful and the guide of the factory spoke great english. It was great to see the tea making in progress and smell the tea in its rawest form. Then, there was the tea tasting. The first couple teas come free while the others cost money to taste. All the teas are great and they bring out an additional rare (we don't know if it actually was) tea for us to try. This tea was 150 USD per kilo....the tea plantation was wide, beautiful and spacious. The tea ladies always beckon you over for photos (and tips). Overall, a wonderful tea plantation and I would recommend coming here.
title: Wonderful example of a tea plantation!

body: Stunning nature surrounds this old tea factory, which is still in full activity. The tours around the factory gives you a good insight in the process of tea making, and makes you humble to every glass of tea you drink thereafter. Also, seeing the hard work of the tea picking ladies, makes you wonder why the tea are not more expensive, and you really wish someone would increase their income a bit. If you take a picture with them, be wise enough to give them a few hundred rupees - they will appreciate the added income
title: Interesting tea factory in beautiful surroundings

body: We had a tour of this tea factopry during our 6 day tour of Sri Lanka. The two, of us were taken round by a very knowledgeable young lady who was able to answer all of our questions. Unfortunately photography isn't allowed inside the factory but I did manage to get one picture which gives you an idea of what it's like
title: Very interesting and free tea at the end

body: The tour of the production facilities is 500 rupees each which I don't think is unreasonable. It was an informative session and there was no hard sell as mentioned in other reviews. In fact it was a bit of an effort to get a tasting and to buy. Views from the location are lovely and all in all well worth an hour or so.
title: Interesting visit to find out how your cup of tea is produced

body: Had a nice 20 minute tour round the factory (note: machinery operates only at night). The tea house could do with having a larger outside terrace to enjoy the plantation views whilst sampling the different teas. Also had a wander through the plantation for some good photo ops with/of the tea pickers.
title: Interesting tea factory tour

body: Dropped by on the way from the Horton plains and weren't disappointed. A nice short tour in the plant with a cup of tea afterwards made the end of the day. One can crop the tea leaves as well but we were unlucky - it started to rain once we set off.
title: Nice short tour

body: We all had to have a picture of us in our green aprons you have to wear for the tour. The tour was nice - some very old equipment. Interesting how the different teas are made. Nice cup of tea on the deck overlooking a great view.
title: Pleasant Experience; Great views

body: Its a short briefing on the flow of making tea. Factory have its specialty as i read in google. It was interesting and fun. A cup of tea as a complimentary before visit the factory. The view of tea estate was awesome! We met an estate worker while taking picture. Worker are so friendly but someone take for granted asked us to paid the worker because we taking their picture.
title: Fast and short

body: Pleasant enough guided tour although not so much to see unless you come after 11.30 when the first tea comes in from the fields. Photography not permitted! Why not? Management policy apparently. Seriously? What’s the secret. A visit to a tea plantation last year in Kerala was much more animated and entertaining because they made sure to have a small batch of tea being crushed, rolled and dried specially for the fee paying visitors. Tea shop not impressive but maybe they’re more interested in selling by the sack at market than by the packet to tourists. I missed opportunity alas
title: No photos please!

body: The guide could not have cared less. Shortest tour possible. Couldn't even be bothered giving us a cup of tea. AND had to pay for the "privilege". Much better options elsewhere - and no charge!
title: Better option abound

body: Quick run through the production plant followed by two samples of tea to taste. Then you must buy.I was hoping to visit the tea plantation, but that was not part of the tour -perhaps due to the inclement weather.Not bad, fairly educational, wouldn't have felt too bad about missing this one.
title: Cool guide though..

body: Visited this tea plantation, whist staying at Nuwara Eliya, during our recent tour of Sri Lanka. Sited in old buildings with old machinery, built in the 50s, we were taken on an interesting 30 minute tour,which gave us a good insight into the basic process of what happens from the time the leaves are brought in from the fields, til they are graded and bagged up to be sent to the tea auctions in Columbo. For some unknown reason, not allowed to take photos during the tour. At the end of the tour there are photo opportunities outside and a chance to sample one of their products. There is a shop where you can purchase their tea, but only in large bags, so not worth the bother. Company could do with a PR overhaul, but a pleasant morning nevertheless.
title: Informatory and interesting tour

body: Enjoyable tour of the factory with an informative guide.The ticket for 200r was very reasonable as it also included cup of tea at the end.I wanted to buy some tea however they only came in large boxes so would be great if they had smaller packaging.
title: Lovely estate

body: An interesting guided tour of the factory followed by a cup of their tea. Only one of their products was available to sample as part of the price. It would have been good to sample other blends as we had done at other tea fctories. Price was 200 Rupees, which was reasonable
title: good insight into the production of tea

body: The tour was excellent throughly explained how the tea was made from start to finish. Would recommend
title: Excellent English with unreal tea

body: Good tour and an interesting insight into how tea is picked and prepared for packaging. Also has great views of the tea estate and a nice place to relax and drink tea (what else)
title: Interesting well worth while

body: We visited the factory with a group and there is no doubt the surrounding area is stunning and everyone is very pleasantI was struck by the emphasis their signs made about how ethical they areI am reliably informed that the pickers are paid only 500 SLR a day - the equivalent of A$5 and not paid if they are sickOur guide was so ill she had not have sit down breaks so she would not collapseThis same multi national company still has its office workers using a typewriter with carbons and a manual ledger!
title: Beautiful but are they really ethical?

body: Short (15 min) visit to the factory for 200 LKR per person with a free cup of tea afterwards on a terrace with beautiful view. Our guide looked little bit annoyed. Not allowed to take pictures inside. It is easily reachable by public bus from the city centre (around 25 LKR per person, 15min). You can also take a walk from here to the Lover's Leap watterfall.
title: Short visit

body: We paid £26.71 per person for 6 people for a private tour. The tour company didn't realise it was a public holiday and so there were no pickers on site and the factory wasn't working. There were people on site who greeted us and actually did give us a tour but, not realising we had pre-booked the visit, they said it would cost us SLR200 each - i.e. approximately £1! So - in essence, we paid £25 for a very expensive taxi ride from our hotel to the tea plantation approximately 3 km away! You can turn up at the Pedro Tea Plantation at any time and be given a tour for SLR 200 and the price of a Tuk Tuk from town. Having said that, the tour was very interesting.
title: A great visit but a huge rip off by the tour company!

body: There is no signage to this effect, but you buy your ticket (Rs. 200) in the nicely located tea shop. It took a while to get to it, as people line up to ask for prices of the various tea packages. Apparently, management does not want to put the prices on the shelves, but rather have each customer approach the cashier to ask. The entrance ticket is amusing. There's a list of admonishments about proper behavior in the factory, including "Do not waste time inside the Factory."After a short wait we got an apron to put on, and joined a large group on the tour. We were about 20 visitors, too many to always hear the guide. She spoke good English, but sometimes her voice was drowned out by the machinery.The best part of the visit was the nice cup of tea on the terrace overlooking the lovely plantation
title: Lovely plantation, but some room for improvements

body: We took the factory tour with a knowledgeable guide. The process really is visible and makes you start to think twice about what goes into our staple cups of tea. The tea pickers have back-breaking work, nevertheless they are happy to welcome you to their world. You can get a nice selection of teas from the shop - without any pressure selling.
title: Fascinating insight into tea production.

body: The plantation is very beautiful and you can also visit by your own walking through the fields. The visit at the factory does not cost so much but it's really too short and at the end we had just a cup of tea (same for everybody, you cannot choose). You can buy tea, but the prices are a little bit higher than in other stores.
title: Nice but too short visit

body: The tour guide from the tea factory has strong accent. It's very hard to understand what she said. The facilities inside the factory are good though. However, the souvenir shop was disappointing. Very few options and no price tag there. Also they use special names for different types of tea so even harder to know what types of tea they are. The only advantage is this tea factory is not too far. We have been to Bluefield tea garden and ceylon tea museum in Kandy. Those are much better places to buy tea in terms of varieties and prices.
title: Nice facilities but hard to understand the guide

body: The guided tour is about 40 minutes and it costs 200 rp per person. At the end you can have a cup of tea.It's interesting if you haven't visited one already. The area all around it's very nice and you can walk around the tea plantations!
title: interesting tour and good tea

body: We didn't try excursion there as it costs 300 rupees and we visitrd Bluefield earlier for free. But we really enjoyed the tea plantation view downhill (not such impressive like Lipton's seat but also good).
title: Very beautiful

body: Unfortunately the size of the tour group (about 20) was too large for the factory tour guide to manage However, the tour was still interesting in terms of the process of making tea from growing to packaging for the market Tea can be purchased at very reasonable prices.
title: Interesting but avoid a large tour group

body: Lovely tour of a tea factory with beautiful views and excellent service... and you get to wear a super sexy outfit to boot!
title: Very lovely tour!

body: Really interesting and informative tour is very workwhile. Explains a lot about the industry how tea is made and the history
title: Worthwhile

body: It's not a big thing, give yourself an hour or two max. But it's a lovely little trip very informative of tea production and cup of tea thrown into the mix for 200 rupees. So can't complain.
title: Lovely little tour

body: Even though the factory was not working (tea production occurs at night here) the guided tour was very informative. The tea rooms are quite nice and offer great views out over a picturesque section of the plantation. The cup of tea was lovely also!
title: Informative tour and lovely plantation

body: It’s a pity that the group sizes are so big.We were shown around by a very sweet lady but unfortunately we couldn’t hear a word she said, due to the noise of the machinery. the gardens are pretty, and it was interesting to look around the factory but overall we felt that they should have more but small tour groups.
title: Average - busy and hard to hear guide

body: To learn how to produce Tea, to understand the work environment in a Tea factory, to understand a little bit more about the plucking of Tea as Well the value chain to the end-consumer. Great and interesting. Pedro seems to be a small and regular production unit, extending with guided Tours, show room, and Tea testing, offering a small range of its products.
title: Great to see Tea production and put IT in its conceptual reference

body: One of the good factory visits and tea plantations. Reach there early before 9 AM to see the tea processing in action. Its ok to also go there later during the day, the tour person will walk you around the factory. Its a good educational tour for the kids.
title: Worth a Visit

body: Paid 200 LKR for the factory tour which the staff told us would take 20 minutes. The machines weren't operating during our visit and we were completely fine with it. The tour took only 10 minutes and the guide wasn't knowledgeable at all. Everyone who left good reviews must have gotten a different guide. When I asked questions, she seemed very annoyed and was just hurrying us to get out of the tea factory to quickly end the tour. The guide is a local woman who is quite short and skinny (if you must know to avoid her). After the tour, they will serve you a cup of tea and it took them 20 minutes and after asking multiple times to serve us our tea. Very bad experience overall! Teas on sale are overpriced too. Other travellers we met who visited blue fields said that was really nice so perhaps check that out instead of Pedro. Bluefields offer free tour too I think! Avoid Pedro at all cost!
title: Don't bother visiting!

body: The half hour tour costs 200 rupees and takes you through the workings of the factory. The guide was very honest and answered all questions including what wages the workers received. Interesting to learn that the grades of tea are sold at auction in Colombo to companies that then add flavours to the basic tea. You are served a good cup of tea either before or after the tour - no milk provided! Great you can walk through the tea plantations which are lovely.
title: Interesting to Visit

body: The friendly guides at the tea factory give you a reasonably comprehensive tour of the tea drying and preparation process. You end up with, what else, a nice cup of tea and it was actually one of the nicest cups of tea I've ever had. A good learning experience.
title: A Lesson In Tea

body: Nice tea shop. Offers guided tours in the tea factory. At the end of the tour you are served a cup of tea in the café with a nice view. You can take walk in the hills.
title: Beautifully located nice tea café with a great view

body: Guide was very knowledgeable and was focused on explaining the tea making process rather than selling tea!
title: Interesting demonstration on how tea is made.

body: Generally good Tea Factory and Explain also good. Helpful staff and they served a Good Tea as well. Tea Field is good and well maintained.
title: Good Tea Factory in N'Eliya

body: There are nice views of the tea plantation but they can be had for free from the side of any road in the region. Our half hour 200 rupee pp tour took about 10 minutes and our guide clearly didn’t want to be there. I also found the tea at the end to be weak. Not a highlight for the trip.
title: Pretty view, disappointing tour

body: We were greeted with a hot cup of team (no milk or cookies) but it was refreshing. It requires a small fee to enter inside the factory. Unfortunately we visited it on Sunday so we could not see if live but we still received a guided tour of the factory inside and how tea is made .
title: Good to visit

body: Short but informative tour in a lovely location - very good value for money and a lovely cup of tea, too. Shop a little pricey.
title: A lovely cup of tea!

body: We had a very short, but still interesting tour in the fabric with the basic information about the producing of tee. Afterwards you get a couple of tee (no need to pay extra).
title: Interesting short visit with a cup of tee afterwards

body: Nice guided visit to understand the process of making tea. After the visit you can walk in the plantations. It would have been nice to have a tea tasting at the end, as the visit is not free.
title: Nice visit

body: Happendix to visit Petroleum tea factory as I need to show its to a freind of mine.They give a trip around the factory and show you how does your tea make.Knowledgeable guides are provide and very nice organized factory.
title: How does your tea make

body: An enjoyable guided tour around an authentic tea factory. All the equipment is on display and the guide explains what its used for, though what is operating depends on the time of day. The cup of tea at the end of the visit is outstanding. Be aware that you can't take photographs in the factory though.
title: Authentic Tea Factory

body: Since we arrived together with the westerner groups we, can see the favoritism in entertaining guests by the staff.
title: Beautiful view

body: We got to the tea plantation and the ladies at the counter told us that the machines were off, so if we wanted to, we could still pay to enter but no tour was going to be offered because the production had finished. We hung out at the lounge and had a cup of tea but it's a level of poverty tourism that I am not comfortable with. All you can see are the tea plantations and the women that work there. If you read a little bit about it, you'll realize that these women are very underpaid. So you end up sipping a cup of tea looking down on the workers from a viewing deck. Not really my kind of thing to do, so I'll just advice you to avoid it altogether. The tea plantations in themselves are beautiful-ish. They're green trees... there are only so many pictures you can take of green trees.
title: Avoid it.

body: Good place to visit, you are taken round the factory to see the process. You get to try some tea on the verandah.Good little shop to buy the different teas.Staff were lovely
title: Learn the history of tea growing

body: The tour is short and I would have wanted a bit more info about the history and cultivating of the tea.
title: Nice short tour.

body: Non operational in the morning. Opening Hours: 8.30 AMTicket: LKR 200/- with one cup of teaIf you don't want to visit the factory, you can still visit the tea plantation without any charges. You can tip the workers in the plantation if you like. The hike in the fields in amazing.
title: Amazing View, Pictorial

body: Should only visit this place if you have never been on a tea factory tour before. The guide was not very enthusiastic and could not communicate very well in English/answer questions that were not in the part of her script. The factory tour itself was very short and not very informative. Since the factory operates only at night we couldn't see any machine working or the end product from a particular machine. Maybe they should have kept samples from each stage for visitors to understand the various processes better. Nonetheless the view from their tasting area balcony was really nice and you were welcome to walk amongst the tree bushes
title: Average

body: We had a good, informative, good English speaking tour round Pedro tea factory. Tour was not free as like in other tea factories but ticket was not expensive. They took us through each stage of the tea making process answering all our questions along the way
title: Good, well explained tour round Pedro tea factory

body: I really enjoyed a brief but informative visit and was happy to see a working factory and the tea making process in action.My new found knowledge will allow me to make more informative selections in the future and I will enjoy the taste even more now knowing how much hard work goes into my daily cuppa.There are numerous tea plantations in this area and many factories I can't imagine they vary much so suggest you pick whats is on route and convenient.
title: Just my cup of tea !

body: The tea factory is among a huge tea plantation. They take you on the tour in groups, while waiting for your turn or after the tour you can relish their complimentary tea drink. There is an fee of 200lkr that is charged, so in case you plan on visiting other places in Nuwara Eliya then one of the bigger tea plantations would be a better option since the tours here dont have charges.
title: Great introduction to tea making

body: A good insight into how demanding tea picking and processing really is. Thank you to the excellent guide who showed us round and answered our questions really well.
title: A must

body: If you are after a substantial tea plantation and factory tour this isn't it, but if you want a quick half hour look inside a factory and cup of tea for 200RS this will do! Our guide was friendly, knowledgeable and some great English. Shame it couldn't be more substantial and feature tea tasting or this would be a winner
title: Basic tour but good value

body: Very interesting. Tour takes about 15 minutes and cost 200rupes per person. Tea reasonably priced if looking for tea purchases.
title: Tea tour

body: We visited two tea factories, one of them was "Pedro". The place is very nice, attention is excellent and you can have a complete vie of the tea process production. Very convenient to understand how it arrives to your cup.
title: Interesting place

body: As I am engaged in the tea sector ,I was much interested about this place but when I tasted the cup of tea I got much dissatisfied as they offered us a cup of tea made of Tea "DUST" thats one of the low cost tea which tastes awful and I totally disappointed with this experience. But I must say the view through the tea shop was quite nice but i went there for tea so if you are looking for great cup of tea ..sorry ,thats would not be the place for such.
title: Poor quality Tea

body: My fiancé said that he felt sorry for taking me to this place. Number one, the service was delayed and we felt ignored. Then to make things really bad, the tea was hopeless. No aroma, no color and it was utterly tasteless. Having so many tourists in the facility, the ladies washroom didn't have any toilet rolls, no hand washing soap and hand towels to dry. Hayleys, what a shame. And please don't put water in the soap dispenser. Disgusting.
title: Utterly disappointed.

body: The tour of the Old Tea Factory was good for those who have yet to visit one, the guide was informative and took time to explain. At the end of tour, you get a free cup of tea at the visiting lounge that has a fantastic view of the Pedro tea estates. We paid Rs200/pax for an afternoon well spent.
title: Educational

body: It was quick and short visit at the Tea Factory. It was good to see the machines and understand the process of making tea.In the end i manage to buy the finish product at their store in the same area. Although the machines were not working at the time of my visit at least I was able to see how the tea making process in reality. Its a good learning experienced and one of a kind. I visited the tea plantation as well along the road. Very nice atmosphere all green everywhere.
title: Worth to visit if you are a tea lover

body: The visit was very quick and hard to understand. Machines are not working during the visit because they work only in night time. They offer a very good cup of tea after the visit, and you can buy tea also but it's expensive. We preferred the visit of Dambatenne tea factory in Haputale.
title: Too quick!

body: Wonderful visit set in a wonderful area. Staff friendly and a great tour around the working tea production. Tastings offered of various teas and the opportunity to purchase. Really enjoyed the tour and very well explained how teas are dried and prepared. Highly recommended and thank you for allowing the public to visit.
title: Holiday/ tour

body: Good tour, very short but explain everything well. Interesting to see inside the factory and you can try the tea at the end. Only 200rupees
title: Well worth a visit

body: A tea plantation must be visited if you are in the area. We visited Pedro Tea Factory. Our guide was informative. We were able to see the different stages of tea processing, even though only some areas of the factory were working that day. You really don't need to see all the stages, as they are well explained and samples of the different types of tea are available to examine.You can taste a cuppa at the end of the tour and even wander in the beautiful plantation and take photos. If you do take a picture of a worker, offer them a bit of money. These women only earn $5 a day if they meet their quotas. It's back-breaking work.
title: Eye opener

body: Make sure before you pay for the tour that you check that it actually is a production day. We payed only to find it was not even in operation that day. It was informative even though it wasn't running.
title: They can be sneaky!

body: Not being much of a tea drinker, I found the factory tour interesting and informative. But what fascinated me more were the tea pickers who worked 8 hours a day with a daily goal of picking 18 kilograms a day, all for less than $5 USD.
title: Informative

body: Good place for a walk. Wandering amongst the tea fields and up to the waterfall was a tealightful experience. Went to get a cuppa after and it came with a free tour (200rps). Tour was short but informative and guide was pleasant. Sat down salivating in anticipation of our post tour beverage but unfortunately it failed to materialise. Asked the waitress twice but it appears it takes more time to make a cuppa than it does to dry and process tea. We sacked it off and went to town for lunch.
title: Came for a cuppa...

body: There are several competing tea factories that are vying to be the top tourist draw of tea country (massive hotels, all the trappings). This one, while perfectly well set up for tourists, is clearly still mainly in the business of processing tea. They have a nice reception area, and start you off with a cup of delicious local product. Then they take you on a very informative tour, on which pictures are inexplicably forbidden (most of the machinery appears to date back to the early industrial revolution, I can't imagine a picture or two would disclose any top secrets but oh well). Guide books say nothing is going on because they do all their processing at night, but I actually saw this as an advantage: no interference, we could walk around and not get in anyone's way. Our guide was very knowledgeable. Strongly recommended!!
title: Basic and Informative

body: Machines were not working when we did the tour. It was short, but it gives you an idea about the proces. It only costs 200 rupees, including a cup of tea. I would do it in combination with Lover's Leap falls.
title: Short tour, but okay

body: We were not so impressed with the tour at this factory. First of all the factory was not in action. I guess because it was a Sunday. So you look at a bunch of machines and try to figure out how it works. The tour leader was very hard to hear because of the noise of cleaning the machines. The good thing is that Pedro works in a very friendly way for the environment, fair trade and so on. The tour itself was however not so great.
title: Average, there must be better tea factories

body: I don't think it's worth it, but it is just 200 roepies. You will guided through the trees factory, she will tell something about the price of producing tea. But her English is not really good, it's a script. You can't understand it, it think Google helps you more about the proces.
title: Not worth it

body: I visited 02 times to this place.Beautiful Sorrounding.Guides explain about tea process A - Z.Worth to Visit.
title: Amazing Tea Plantation Tour

body: Nice tea factory to visit. Thought I preferred the Ceylon Tea Museum near Kandy. But if you are in Nuwara Eliya and you didn't already visited something like that, don't hesitate it's worth a visit. The view there is also really nice.
title: Nice tea visit

body: The tea plantation has beautiful scenery and perhaps walking around the grounds was better than the tour itself.When we visited, the factory was not running, due to the poor weather meaning the tea was not grown correctly. However, we were only told this after our tour had begun which we found slightly cheeky. The tour guide was very lovely and informative however, and the tour is finished with a very refreshing cup of their own tea. They were then very helpful in booking us a cab to the train station.Would definitely recommend to anyone staying in Nuwara Elia.
title: Good value

body: Worth a visit. Old tea company- see how tea is made and the different qualities of tea. Tour of the factory. Not too comercial.
title: Short trip - see how tea is made

body: We stopped here for a couple of hours on our way from the station to our hotel in Nuwara Eliya. This plantation was one of the first and we given a nice cup of BOP before a guided tour of the whole process from picking to packing. Very informative and interesting even for our eleven year old son. We were also able to wander the hillsides and get close to pickers afterwards which was great.
title: Interesting tour of the plantation

body: The visit to the tea estate was somewhat delayed but the tour guide was very patient and it was encouraging to see how she was self developed. The lack of water and toilet paper in the toilets was a little disconcerting.
title: Very educative and worthwhile

body: Of all the tea factories, this one felt most genuine, not a tourist trap at all!Totally recommended, interesting overview of a tea factory's ins and outs, set to a beautiful view, with a lovely cup of tea as a finale!
title: Not too touristy

body: Surrounded by beautiful tea plantations, the Pedro Tea Factory was a great place to visit. We had a lovely friendly tour guide who took us round the factory, although by the time we got there, it wasn't actually in use. Our guide was knowledgeable and explained everything really well, and the tea at the end was a lovely treat!
title: Really interesting!

body: Thanks to our guide who was knowledgeable we left with a good understanding of the Tea Making process. The factory is clean, staff are helpful and efficient and the complementary Tea is fabulous! 200 rupees and the best tour we did!
title: Informative tour of the Tea Factory

body: Nice quite old factory. Very interesting to see how tea is produced. Beautiful tea gardens with many traditionally clothed women.
title: Must have been

body: Very poor guided tour as only the basics of tea manufacturing was explained. The floors were wet and unclean. At the tea boutique the tea was overpriced. Nothing of the history of this great estate was shared. The guides though were courteous and polite. They need to be supplied with more information.
title: Tour

body: The tea at the end of the tour was surprisingly refreshing! The tour was a bit shorter than we expected. Also we went on a day when the factory was technically closed so we didn't get to see things in action - pick your day wisely.
title: Insightful

body: This factory is rich in history. I must admit that the factory is very well run and please do join the tour, which is very informative. At the end of the tour, you will be served with a cup of very fragrant tea. The estate itself is beautiful....very green with a panaromic view of the area. I have visited a couple of tea factories in my life and in fact, this is the best of the lot. It is a "must-see" when you are in Nuwara Eliya
title: Top Class Tea Factory In Nuwara Eliya

body: I was a bit disturbed that they call these factories plus staff housing "estates" when in reality its modem plantations. Please ask your guide for more info... they don't hide information about the setup of these "estates". All staff seem happy and at peace, grateful even, for the accommodations and the work. Please take the factory tour - very informative - from start to finish. You learn the entire tea process. The best part is learning how tea "tasters" from all over Sri Lanka have such a delicate palate they can identify any tea from any region by taste and smell. I love the sustainability museum at the end of the tour. It's nice to see that such hard work and production is done with the environment in mind.
title: For all tea lovers

body: We visited the tea factory in August 2016. It was lovely and very informative! Unfortunately, we arrived at the factory the day after Poya day, so there was no tea to process. I think the whole tour lasted about 45 minutes and you get a free cup of tea to taste afterwards.
title: Great visit! Remember not to go after Poya day

body: First we were treated to a lovely cup of tea in the waiting area. We were given aprons and then taken on an informative tour through the tea factory. We saw different stages of tea production and were explained just how time consuming and precise a process it is.
title: Interesting Enough

body: Nearby the town and a great place to spend an hour or so during a rainy monsoon morning. Pleasant tea café and beautiful views; interesting to see how tea is processed (but be warned going upstairs is one of the hottest experiences ever -- the warm air from the drying process drifts upwards and literally a bit hard to breathe)!
title: Friendly Guide through Working Tea Factory

body: The walk through the tea factory followed by the cup of tea is a wonderful experience. The guides take you around the place which costs LKR 200 (only cash). Your tea comes with the mildest variant that they produce so it's something that you need to keep in mind
title: A very wonderful time spent

body: They first take you on a tour around the place showing you how tea leaves are taken through various processes and result in the final product-tea powder.After that they give you a hot cup of tea which is very soothing and refreshing.They also sell tea packets freshly prepared in the factory at a nominal price.Overall a good way to spend 1 hr!!!
title: The process of manufacturing of tea is explained very well

body: Had a nice cup of tea - Lover's leap which is only sold in Pedro tea factory. Visiting tea factory is okay, we were guided by a Tamil women with detailed history and tea making process. The only point is photography is not allowed - which is not forbidden in other tea factories. It's the nearest tea factory you can reach from center, take bus in bus stand (ask them which bus to go, 10 Rs and journey is less than 10mins) After visiting finish, you could take a easy walk downward to city center , which only takes 40 mins with 3-4km.
title: Soft and cozy tea factory

body: We stopped and had a tour of this working tea factory which was really interesting. It has been in operation for many years and had some of the old equipment around. Our guide was interesting but I had hoped that we could have a tasting of the different teas. Maybe next time.
title: Working tea factory

body: It is a good experience to go inside the factory and know the processes of the tea industry and have a cup of tea in some beautiful terrace seeing the tea plantation and finally purchasing a good and cheap packs of some kinds of tea
title: New experience

body: One can learn all about tea making in this beautiful tea factory. A guided tour takes you around the tea factory and the guide explains to the group all about the process involved from the time the tea leave is plucked to the entire process of drying and the end product which we drink!
title: An interesting morning spent at the tea factory

body: Loved it, smelt the tea as soon as we arrived :-)Was an interesting tour, that was very interesting & makes you think of those ladies working so hard each day for such little pay!
title: Perfect short day trip

body: Me my wife n daughter enjoyed this place.It was amazing to see the process and tea estate was very beautiful 👍🏻
title: Nice,knowledgeable and beautiful place

body: Staff is very friendly and ready to help visitors. very old tea factory established in 19th century.
title: friendly staff

body: well worth a visit to see the different teas produced and how it is made. Guide was extremely knowledgeable and interesting
title: an excellent place to learn about tea

body: Great to see how these places operated in the past. They produce great tea and are very willing to share their experience and history.
title: Working tea factory

body: Pedro tea factory is near Nwara Eliya and not too far from Heritance Tea Factory. The guide spoke perfect English and the tour of the working factory very interesting. You can see all phases of tea production. There is a small shop where you can buy their local tea and you can taste it.
title: Very interesting

body: I visit with my guest to buy tea. Then i wait 1/2 hour for factory visit so return from factory wait 1/2 hour again for tea taste. Very bad restaurant area toilet smel always. After buy tea wait 1/2 hour paid bill one lady is working issuing factory entrace ticket explain tea cash collect. I dont know why managemet sleep like this i m giving instruction all visitors dont go for time weast.
title: Westing time

body: Our tour guide did the best she could with the English language and I guess they do the tour at 20 min duration, that really is not enough.there is a huge history in tea and incredible variations in the process used to obtain final product. I was left with many questions.Otherwise friendly staff and pretty environment
title: Tour too short on time and info

body: The walk in the plantation, though unassisted is the best thing for those looking for serenity and quiet! Lush green, with majestic pineladen mountains for a backdrop, it cannot get calmer!The tea shop has awesome and courteous staff, and amazing tea. Prices very well against the commercial ones we stopped at on the way-at peradeniya! This one is simple, crisp, and warm!! Cant miss.
title: Ammazing!

body: I enjoyed visiting Pedro Tea factory and it was really informative visit . The tour took around an hour . They greeted us with a free cup of tea that we enjoyed at their amazing terrace and then the tour began, After the tout they offer us six types of tea and we chose three types to buy. If you are travelling with kids , the visit will be really nice to them.
title: very intersting factory

body: We really enjoyed the tour. The lady was so proud of her culture and heritage, it was lovely.Nice grounds and walks in the area.
title: Proud staff, lovely grounds

body: Went here in the afternoon. No tour available. Shop is small, offers some tasting. Tea is quite nice actually. Not worth going out of your way to get her; if you are in the area, ok.
title: Not much to see; night time ops

body: It's easy to get here either by local bus (just say you want to get off at Pedros) or by tuk tuk 300 each way. The tour is 200 & takes 20mins. It's not the most informative & you can't take photos, but it is good to see the old machinery & it does give you a feel about tea production. At the end you do get a cup of tea, which wasn't the best I've tasted so didn't tempt me to buy their tea at the shop. Definitely worth doing & across the street is the start of lovers leap walk.
title: Quick guide to tea

body: Small charge to look round (200 rupees per person). Kitted out with hats and aprons and then shown each stage of production as a small family group which was lovely... no big tour. Only takes about 30mins. Very hot in the baking area but thoroughly interesting seeing each step. Welcome cuppa at the end!
title: Well presented tour

body: Given the importance of tea to Sri Lanka it seemed odd not to try and learn a little about the history of the industry, the people who work in it and the journey it makes from the beautifully cultivated hillsides to our daily brew. This tour, which took around 2 hours touches on most of the those topics. Having been warmly received in a very modern facility, we were each given a gown to wear and ushered off in a small group tour of the facility. This starts with learning about the picking process and the pickers, moves to the drying and a discussion about what makes each type or grade of tea, to the rolling, sorting and packing. Our tour guide was a 4 th generation lady who was excellent and handled even the toughest question with an interesting answer. We liked her a lot as it was obvious what she was doing mattered to her. With the tour over you get to enjoy a nice cuppa. If you are in the area you really should do one of these tours and this one is pretty decent.
title: Pleasant few hours learning about tea picking and production in Sri Lanka

body: We toured the facility which has been in business for more than 150 years. We watched the process from collection to drying and processing leading to the final products (no pictures allowed). We got to taste and purchase the real Sri Lankan tea. People were very pleasant and the views over the tea plantations beautiful. A must stop if you are in the area.
title: Want to learn about tea? This is the place!

body: english was ok, but the guide was not very motivatedthe group was hugemost people did not get what was saidthere are better visits!!
title: overcrowded tour by a not very motivated guide

body: Thanks to the Pedro tea factory staff.It was very informative tour inside of the factory (20 minutes).
title: Good place, tasty tea.

body: Nice to see how they made tea, tour is not long but interesting, you can not take pictures inside the building.You can buy tea at the factory
title: Nice to see how they made tea

body: If you are a Tea drinker, this is a must place to visit. The factory visit gives you a glimpse of how your favourite tea is made and tasting it. They offer some of their teas for free to try them but others are just for buying.
title: A beginners guide to teat manufacturing and tasting

body: We had a nice tour and learned a lot about tea. Try to visit on Tuesday through Friday. On Monday there is not tea to process since they don't pick on Sunday- something we learned to our chagrin.
title: Nice factory

body: The history of the manning of tea plantations is rather sobering but things have improved. We really enjoyed being shown around by a knowledgeable Tamil Tea worker. We then wondered through the plantation learning about which leaves are used for different tastes. As the plantations are high up it is nice and cool and very lovely.
title: An insight into an every day beverage.

body: This is a must. It is so interesting and the staff are really nice. Walking around it's hard to believe that they still produce the tea with all the old machinery.
title: Really interesting

body: Good tour around the factory and good to know the tea process... inside the factory is really dirty and tea spilled all over the place, my wife and kid found it difficult to walk...
title: Not bad

body: Unfortunately the weather wasn't the best on the day.The gentleman who gave the tour seemed very passionate about the place, and provided some interesting facts. Not sure that I would have come here if I wasn't on a group tour, knowing the living and work conditions of tea plantation tea pickers. Though this place had many posters stating how they house and help their workers.
title: Visit to tea factory

body: They run guided tour every 30 minutes there and it is a small tea factory. Guide was very good, giving us a good overview of the process, but it remains quite small
title: Small homely tea factory

body: Well worth a visit if you are in the area, the tour takes you through the various tea making processes and, of course, a chance to buy tea at the end. Very interesting.
title: Fascinating tour of tea factory

body: We visited on a Sunday so sadly the plant was not in operation, but we were still able to have a tour of the factory. The tour was quick, but better than 2 other two estates toured in Nuwara Eliya as they provided more information on the entire process than others. Don't expect too much when touring as tours typically last 10-15 mins.
title: Quick tour, best of 3 estates

body: First, take in the great views of the adjacent lush countryside and then take the tour which explains all one needs to know about the history and production of tea in Sri Lanka! The staff guide was most knowledgeable and responsive to questions.
title: Very informative and interesting in a lovely setting

body: The Tea factory offers a tour explaining the picking and processing of tea leaves, and has a store to purchase their tea products. The tour costs Rs. 200 per person. The tea is processed at night to take advantage of the cooler temperatures, and so the processing operation (except ambient drying) was not operational during the tour. Besides, the tour guide was not very clear about description of the process. A cup of tea is offered at the end of the tour. In my opinion, charging a fee to tour a non-operational facility makes this factory unwelcome as a place to visit, when there are so many other factories in the area.
title: Large Tea Factory offering a Tour for a fee

body: Although a paid attraction, this is well worth the spend (200) with a professional guide and freedom to roam the tea plantation afterwards. Met with some tea pickers who were very happy to pose for pics (a tip will be expected for this) and explained how tghey choose the leaves etc. The Duke of Edinburgh visited this factory in 1954 as the small exhibition of paper cuttings and photos shows - an interesting addition to the tour.
title: Professional Tour

body: We enjoyed our tour of the factory although our guide was a quietly spoken girl. Afterwards, we were given a cup of tea in a pleasant little restaurant. Very nice. Takes about 15-20 minutes to do the tour.
title: Interesting place

body: It is worth a visit as you get to see inside the factory and are taken through the whole tea production process. Then you get a cup of tea to taste and it is delicious. The tour and tea are free and given with the usual lovely Sri Lankan smile!
title: Interesting place

body: We went there by bus for just a few rupees from Nuwara Elya bus station. Nothing special, but nice to see and get a tour through the factory. The tour costs 200 LKR per person and takes around 30 minutes. Afterwards you get a tea in their small shop.
title: Worth a visit

body: After a wonderful train trip into the high country this tour did not in any way live up to our expectations. It was a rushed tour with the explanations of the workings of the plantations and the origins of Sri Lankan tea sadly lacking. We were taken around the facility but ended up with no further knowledge than we had arrived with. We were not shown any tea bushes or how they were picked. Sad to say the least as we had looked forward to this part of our journey.A video would have been altogether more enlightening .
title: Disappointing

body: Nice view from the estate but the girl giving the tour of the factory felt quite uninterested. Informative but with no engagement. Okey. Assume there a more genuine Tea factory options around. No tasting, only one cup served after finishing the stort tour.
title: Short Tea factory tour

body: We enjoyed the factory tour and the history of the very first tea factory in Sri Lanka very clear explanation and then tasting on terrace overlooking the tea plantations better than expected
title: Really enjoyed the history and insight into the Sri Lanka tea industry

body: A very good tea factory, working mainly in the night. The tour costs 200 rupees, but include a complimentary excellent cup of tea, and the plantation grounds are very well tended and magnificent to look at.
title: Very good tea factory

body: The various reviews describing the rush in which the "tour" was made and the one cup of tea to "taste" should really have been a warning. But we thought everybody has a bad day someday, and wanted to give it a try. Bad idea. Badly organized staff, lack of communication among them, being indeed rushed through factory halls where only very few woman and machines were actually working. The lady showing us around spoke complicated to understand and with a very low voice. Heard a bit about the process but nothing at all about what makes a good tea, what are the different variations, about the company, and its (fair??) trade, the working conditions... Nada. After maximum 10min we were "done". Got one single cup of tea, no chance to do a tasting. And guess what, it wasn't even a good tea. Had we had an idea where else to go, we would have done that. So, at least we can warn other future visitors.
title: Not worth the money and effort to go there

body: If you're a tea drinker check this establishment out. The tour of the factory by an informative guide is well worth the time and the short trip out of town. The vistas are beautiful, however the shop only sells several packets of tea at a time, so if space in your luggage is limited you'll be disappointed.
title: A great place to visit.

body: We simply turned up and tours were running pretty much all the time (every 15 minutes roughly, each time enough people we waiting for them to run one), it was 200 LKR each (we visited on 16-02-2017) and the tour rook about 20 minutes. After the tour they gave us free tea to try and we went for a walk around the tea gardens. You can buy all the tea they grow there. The tour was in English.
title: A short but informative tour and great tea

body: Apparently the cycle of picking, drying and generally bashing the leaves into bits is all over by about 09:30. But the factory tour is still open and it is interesting to see the various antique machines standing ready to spring into life next dawn. The tour includes a cuppa in the picturesque waiting area, which is nice.
title: Tea Making? Oh you missed that.

body: Nice to know how our tea is gathered, processed and sent to the auction house in Colombo. Best of all was the cup of tea at the end
title: what else - tea -

body: Very interesting visit here finished with a lovely cup of their own home grown produce! Recommend a visit here.
title: Tea plantation visit

body: you pay a small price and they take you on a tour. There are certain times which I forgot which had the actual processing but I think the process at night and stop in the morning for new batches.
title: very informative on tea making - loved it

body: Very informative although the factory mostly works at night for climatic reasons. It is a pity that they don't sell their own tea after the visit.
title: Interesting

body: The explanation provided by the factory team is very instructive...especially that team shows guests the real-life machinery and the real process they adopt...the team member who led us was a real subject matter expert and talented in explaining and answeting questions..After knowing well the industry and various types pf Tea, it's time to taste an amazing local Tea while enjoying the unlimited Green of this noble plant...spread into big and wide valleys...memorable experience for us and our kids as well..
title: Great Visit, Great Product

body: We had a very interesting morning here, the tour was informative and not too long, the factory still using machinery from the 1950s which are works of art in themselves. From the tea factory it's a good walk to Lovers Leap waterfall where you can see tea pickers at work. It's an easy bus ride from Kandy.
title: Interesting visit, beautiful location

body: On arriving we were given a cup of the plantation tea, which was delicious, and we were able to sit out on the balcony overlooking the plantation and enjoy the morning sunshine and lovely views. The tire was interesting although quite short, I would have liked to also have a chance to learn about how they pick the tea and look after the plants (it focuses on the processing of the tea after it is picked). Still very interesting however. It can be hard to hear the guide on the factory of you have a large group. The factory promotes worker welfare and ethical tea practices, there are interesting signboards in the visitor centre about the factory's history and engagement in UN programmes.
title: Interesting tour

body: -We went as a couple -A free tea at arrival was very nice and is for sale-the factory tour was very cheap and it lasted about 30mins. The lady doing the tour was very nice and the tour was informative-we had a short walk around the tea fields and its beautiful-i would recommend visiting this tea factoryThanksSam
title: Good

body: For 100rp you get a 20min tour of the production process from them delivering the tea from the field to the packaging. Was interesting.
title: If you have the time

body: Pedro is geared up to show parties around a totally functioning tea factory. Good guide but plenty of climbing and no photography allowed. A visit gives you an idea of the whole, very quick process of producing packed tea from fresh leaves, ending with the sobering fact that the guide would have to work two days to earn enough to pay for a packet of the best English Breakfast tea.
title: Pretty rapid

body: Beautiful experience of watching ladies picking tea leaves (very friendly to chat to) walking through fields and understanding the tea process. After the tour a complimentary cup of tea was provided. Very enjoyable tour. Advice to come there before 4pm if you want to see the machines still working.
title: Really enjoyed the visit to Pedro's

body: Lovely cup of tea pn arrival with a beautiful view of the plantation. The tour was informative and the guide was terrific.
title: Lovely visit

body: The place is a working tea factory. They make a real effort to be both welcoming and informative. You get a well explained tour of the whole factory and emerge with a better understanding about tea.
title: Welcoming and interesting

body: I'm sure I would give this a higher score if we had find in a different day (on a group trip so no choice about that). The factory is basically shut on Sundays so nothing is working and you just get a short talk about the process. Would be much more interesting to see it all working.
title: Dont go on a Sunday!

body: Our appointed guide gave us a clear explanation of each step of the process from the tea field to the cup
title: An insight into working tea factory

body: We were a bit disappointed by this tour of the tea estate. Most of the areas of production were not operating and we found the man who was taking us around difficult to understand. He was speaking in English and we were the only people in the group who had English as our first language so I would imagine the other people understood even less.
title: Disappointed

body: i've visited them today and was a great learning experience actually! my guide was a young Sri Lankan lady that had a great knowledge of tea and what goes into prepering a perfect cup. at the end of tje tpur they offer you one of the best orange pekoe i've tasted....
title: lovely no frills plantation!

body: Huge area of tea plantations till your sight can see. One section overlooks the sunset and lake, which is beautiful. Enjoyed walking across the estate.
title: Beautiful lush tea estate!

body: to start with, this tea factory was built in 1880!we did a guided factory tour where we were explained the complete process of segregating, processing and treating tea leaves which is then supplied to all the big Tea brands around the world. we also saw their tea plantations and interacted with tea pickers who taught us which leaves to pick from the plantations.the premises also houses a small tea cafe with a terrace facing plantations and hills, which is quite serene!good for a short visit, Dont forget to carry some sandwiches as there is lack of good eatery around
title: Scenic tea factory and plantations!

body: We visited, when on our tour through Sri Lanka passing by, this tea factory with its old machines, had tour and bought some tea. It is worth to have a visit here - as well as strolling through the plantations - on public ways of course.Nice and beautiful place.
title: Nive Place to Visit

body: Interesting to see the factory, good place to visit in this area but felt it missed out on providing a bit more detailled information.
title: Interesting

body: Amazing place, the best tea plantations in Nuwara Eliya area. Green scenery, overlooking tea and lake, great place to lost yourself in tea bushes
title: Perfect tea plantations with an ambient atmosphere

body: An hour well spent on an introduction into how the Tea Leaf is made into Tea. From plant to the finished product. Well worth a visit
title: Sri Lanka Adventure

body: We went to the factory early in the morning which was a good decision, because we were the only ones. The factory is small so the tour doesn't take a lot of time. I would recommend you to choose any other day except monday, because sunday is non working day and we weren't able to see first and second phase of the process. It was fascinating to see how they still produce tea with the machinery from late 19th century.The only minus was our guide which wasn't very talkative. We were asking her a lot of question and she just gave us short answers.
title: Pleasant walk through the history of tea making

body: Spent an hour being shown around the factory having the process explained to us. This was followed by a taste of their tea in a very pleasant café. Tea was so good I ordered some when I got home. Good way to spend some time.
title: Great cup of tea!

body: The guide gave very good and clear explaination which we can understand. We learnt the different variety of teas. This place is a must to visit when in Nuwara Eliya!
title: Good guide!

body: Our guide had excellent English and understood our intricate questions about the production of tea. This was a nice shortish tour (30mins?) where we could really see what happens at night when the tea is processed. Free cuppa at the end.
title: Great explanation and tour of a working tea factory

body: This place was great, if anything it is underpriced and compared to many places we visited in the country they couldn't triple the entry price to £3 and it would still be just as popular.We got to don trendy aprons so we looked just like the rest of work workers there before infiltrating the plantation! We got to see how tea was made from start to finish although we couldn't take pictures and so Mrs V is going to have to put up with PG tips as opposed to me starting up my own UK based tea production plant from our 3 bed house! What a disappointment!Despite this we really enjoyed the trip as well as the tea we got to try at the end of it.After you visit ask for directions to the waterfall, it's an easy amble or if your mega lazy you can get a tuk tuk.Happy travels,Mr and Mrs V
title: Great place and walk to the waterfall afterwards
