body: We visited with 2 young children and they enjoyed the tour. We were lucky when we arrived as they were just finishing up the processing of the tea and the warmth and smells from the tea were fantastic. The tour was informative but not too informative that it became boring, you moved quite quickly from one station to the next, the guide we got was great. Lovely views over the plantation. Enjoyed a fresh tea complimentary after the tour, doesn't taste like tea I have every experienced before.
title: Fun visit!

body: Gorgeous destination to take in the beauty of the tea fields. Lovely, knowledgeable guide and a refreshing tea served at the end best enjoyed out on the deck in the sun. A worthwhile activity
title: A fun way to spend an hour

body: We really enjoyed our tour here and the tea was great. Very informative. The views were so beautiful around the factory.
title: Fun visit!

body: The tour itself is quite disappointing as the factory works only during the night so the machines are inactive. Nor do you get to see the tea fields up close. So it's more of a 15 minute theoretical lecture on the art of tea making. You don't even get to see the tea leaves across the various stages of manufacturing to try and visualise the process. The tour guide is polite and speaks decent English. We had a really poor experience as at the end of the tour we were just left to our own devices and based on having read previous reviews we knew we were supposed to head back to the tea house for a cup of tea. Ended up waiting for approximately 25 mins and no one even bothered to attend to us. Left the place disappointed and empty handed as we really weren't inclined to pick up any tea from the gift shop after being treated so poorly.
title: Visit only if you have nothing else to do!

body: A good tour of a tea factory, giving an insight into the tea making process. The guide spoke good english and was very informative.
title: Good tour

body: We were there around 9.30 am.Morning is better, less visitors and can enjoy quit a lot.Parking is also easy when you go early.Everyone has a nice and pleasant smiley welcome.Local entrance is Rs.50 and for the foreigners is Rs.200.Have to wear green color Apron to visit inside and a guild comes with visitors and he explains very well how to make tea step by step. Explanation was really good.After the visit they will provide really nice cup of tea and you can sit their front office and enjoy it.There has a very clean washroom and nice surrounding with tea estate,Hills,Mist.. (Sunday workers are not working in factory but you can go and see inside)
title: Worth to Visit

body: We loved taking a long walk through the tea fields, there is a lake you can walk to which is beautiful and, if walking isn't your thing, the views from the tea house at the top are just incredible! Plus their tea is delicious and just what you need to warm you up as it's a bit chilly up there.
title: Incredible views with delicious tea!

body: Enjoyed our visit here , nice cup of tea, interesting tour,no hard sell, sadly the tea picking women get paid a pittance for long hours in the baking sun and its hard to witness such harsh treatment and then forget about it. I'll never take my morning tea for granted again.
title: Interesting

body: Definitely worth a visit. For 200 Rupees per person you get about 30 minutes of explanation while walking through the factory and a cup of tea afterwards. Money/value is good in my opinion.
title: Interesting visit

body: This is an interesting place to go & find out more about the making of black tea in a beautiful setting among some vintage machinery. The guide was excellent - patient & very happy to answer questions. Tips: As production is overnight you don't see much action. No pics inside but great shots from balcony afterwards. Stop close to the factory to snap tea pickers at work
title: Interesting & informative

body: We went to the place with my family i.e my wife, two daughters aged 8 and 12. Finding the place was not difficult and they have the parking. We went there at around 1pm and we were welcome and served with a plain tea which was very good. Ticket was Rs 50/= to visit the factory. We were given green colour apron which I think for food safety. We were guided by their facilitator and he explained the process very well. If you are not familiar with the tea process this is food place to visit special children loved it.
title: Pedro Tea Factory

body: We walked here from our hotel, it was quite a walk but the scenery was beautiful. At first we weren't sure where to go when we entered the tea plantation grounds but we found the ticket counter in the tea shop. Tickets were 200 rupees each. A lady took us round the factory explaining what each machine does and the journey of the tea leaves from picked to packaged. The guide spoke pretty good English and knew enough about the equipment. The equipment was all switched off as the factory process the leaves at night due to the type of tea they make but it was still enjoyable enough. At the end you get a free cup of tea to taste. We walked back passing the waterfalls which was beautiful. Follow our journey on Instagram @twolotllamas
title: Worth a visit

body: We visited the tea factory in November 2016. I found it very upsetting the tea pickers are very poorly paid. We were told by our guide of the tour by the time you are 40 their backs have gone and go no longer work. The machinery is so out of date (no photos allowed of the machinery). I just felt they are like modern day slaves it definitely made me think how lucky we all are with our housing and way off life.
title: i was moved by this factory

body: We really enjoyed our visit to the tea factory. Its very calm and charming place. The lady took us to the factory tour thru all the processes and nicely explained the various tea categories.It ends with a hot cup of BOP tea!
title: Excellent Tea Factory - superb experience

body: It was our third tea factory (we were bored :D) and the guiding thing was like any other, nothing special, only thing we didn't like is that all their production is over night so prepare you won't see much action. Anway, this estate has the most beautiful landscape so far, it is worth going there just for the view and good pictures ;). Take a walk a sit on the balcony sippingh the tea and enjoying the view. Beautiful Sri Lanka, it really is!
title: Beautiful fields

body: Perched on top of a hill a little away from the city center this tea garden is among one of the best in Sri Lanka. With a tour fee of LKR 250 the guide takes you through the factory with its century old machinery which are still in use. The tea produced here is a lovely light one - which you can sample for free. Another quirk about this factory is that they allow you to move very freely among the tea plantation. On a cloudy day this is amazing
title: Amazing Tea Garden

body: A quaint place with lovely ,friendly staff. Amazing how much trouble people go to for us to have a cup of tea :-)
title: Group Trip-Projects Abroad

body: This is not a working factory and therefore not very interesting. They are more interested in selling the tea. Very disappointed. It should be classed as a poor museum.
title: Disappointed

body: We coupled this tour with a hike up to Lovers Leap waterfall. This was a great experience - the tour was very informative and they answered all our questions very well. You also get to sample the tea afterwards. Don't buy the tea from there though, it's a bit too expensive!
title: Informative tour, hike up to lovers leap waterfall

body: When we went there the factory was closed, so we just visited the sales center and bought some items. Some people were going into the factory although it was not functioning at the time. We had to settle for another factory another time.
title: Just visited the boutique

body: It's just a tea factory and there is a catch. They take you for a tour of the factory and show you, in real time, how black tea is processed. At the end , they do serve you tea and you have the opportunity to buy some to take away. Not too bad as loose leaf tea is getting increasingly more difficult to find in some countries.
title: Tea factory tour and sales

body: Pedro Tea Estate is close to Nuwara Eliya - a 10 minute drive maximum. We had a guided factory tour which was quite interesting despite it being presented by a not very interested in us young woman. Afterwards we enjoyed a cup of tea in their tea café overlooking the tea garden. We were allowed to wander through the tea gardens on our own. Allow 1 hour for all. They also have a shop but you have to purchase tea in packs of 3 or 6 which is quite a lot if you have limited luggage room or are still travelling on. I thought this ridiculous and gimmicky to make you have to buy more than you want. Otherwise it's very pleasant to visit.
title: Pleasant visit with some annoyance

body: We did the tour which was very detailed and clear. There is a 500 rupees entrance fee per person and u get a cup of tea at the end. They have a nice collection of tea to buy at their store. A nice place.
title: Nice factory

body: Impressive history. Lovely view from the terrace. Great shop. We bought lots of teas and are enjoying them at home with fond memories.
title: World famous Pedro Estate

body: A tour of the Pedro Tea Factory was quite interesting, but rather rushed. We were the first visitors at 8.00 am. The young guide explained the different stages of how the tea is processed and what the various machinery does. No photos are allowed inside the factory. The actual production occurs during the night so we did not see any of the workers or the machines in action. The views from the outside grounds are lovely. Other tea factories may offer a more comprehensive insight
title: Flying visit

body: This place offers tours of a tea plantation and then a cafe area to sample the products. OK for an hour or so if you are in the area.
title: Quick tour of a tea factory

body: We traveled from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya by train and saw beautiful hills covered with tea plantations. From Nuwara Sliya we took tuk-tuk to Pedro Tea Factory. Factory tour was very short, year was to dry so we couldn't see entire process of tea preparation.View from factory and tea degustation were very nice.
title: We expected much more than we saw.

body: Very informative visit. Unfortunately machinery was being maintained and cleaned when we visited so we did not see it in full production but that is probably a blessing - the machines generate and need a lot of heat to do the drying of the tea. Felt sorry for the staff - very poorly paid compared to our standards.
title: Great introduction to tea industry

body: If you're used to factory tours this a bit different - the end-to-end process (which is interesting) is largely carried out on machinery from the early 20th century. Very interesting visit - and of course you can buy all kinds of tea!
title: Step back in time

body: They have a simple yet complicated tea factory, for a price of 200/- we can get a chance to look around and know how teas are being made, we were unlucky and couldn't see the live process as workers were off duty but the lady who gave us a tour was so good at explaining. And the fun part was we were offered tea made from freshly brewed leaves right after the tour in there main building which is located in a very beautiful place surrounded by nature all over.
title: The Location

body: Its look amazing big mountain around factory near factory there is tea shop you can order tea its frash tea and nice teste
title: Nice view. Behind factory

body: Great activity in Nuwara Eliya, very reasonable price to enter (200 LKR) included a guided tour and free cup of tea. You can also walked around the plantations. Very close to lover's leap waterfall.
title: Tea Factory

body: One of several tea factories I visited in Sri Lanka. Beautiful location, great pictures over the tea plantations. Tour was not overly informative. They were processing leaves at time of visit so it was nice to observe that and get some explanation. All be it rather short. They produce Orthodox (leaves remain somewhat in tact) and CTC (chopped leaves typically for tea bags) tea, the Orthodox production was a bit grey on detail. Nice cuppa afterwards. I would not go out of my way for this Tea factory, if you have been to Mackwoods, Bluefields or what I considered my best visit, Loolecondera Tea Factory then skip this. Pedro did not make my top 5.
title: Morning visit. Quick average tour. Nice views.

body: Really enjoyed this tour of the tea factory led by a very pleasant knowledgeable young lady. We saw the process from arrival of the leaves through to the final packing and got a taste at the end.
title: Very interesting tour

body: My wife and I been to the Pedro Tea Estate and we've enjoyed the tour inside the factory which seemed very organized. The tour guide was very informative and nice with kids. We highly recommend this factory than others due it's view and nicely put tour.
title: Nicely organized tea factory tour

body: For 200 rupees you can take a 30 minute tour around the factory, which is just enough time to see how everything works without getting bored ;-) Best visited in the afternoon when the leaves have been collected and are being processed.
title: Great little tour around a working tea factory.

body: For 200 rupees they offer a visit to the fabric and a cup of tea. The visit was very interesting, but we couldn't take any picture inside and the fabric wasn't working while the visit, so we couldn't see how machines work.Anyway, it's a very good visit to know how tea is produced. And in 30 minueltes you can arrive to Lover's Leap, a very beautiful waterfall nearby.
title: Very nice visit

body: The tour we went on whilst very informative in the manufacture of tea spends no time on the plantation and the plants and the picking process. The tea at the end is nice and walkimg through the plantation makes for a good walk.
title: Good tour

body: We were told that the tea processing is only at night so we were expecting to see only machines and stuff like that. However, we came at around 8am and we still saw some processes and how different kind of tea is being made and how does it look like. At the end of the tour we had some nice tea on a bench in the balcony of the tea shop where we could see a lovely view of tea plantations. We enjoyed that.
title: Interesting

body: Love this place, we had a tour around the factory and saw the process of tea. afterwards had tea at the balcony, facing beautiful tea plantation. And view of nuwara Definitely Worth the visit.
title: Amazing !!

body: This active tea factory can be visited to get a better inside on how tea is produced. There is busses going from and to nuwara eliya which stop right in front of the tea factory! The tour itself is about 30 minutes and after that you can have a cup of tea and wonder around the tea plantations! Beautiful scenery and entrance price is fair at 200rp!
title: Nice insight in an active tea factory

body: We dropped in here for an early morning tour. Sadly they were just cleaning all the machinery up and the tour lacked some spark.
title: Tour visit

body: Very quick tour largely showing dormant machinery so not exactly the most stimulating time. It is patently a very old and established company and there should be some interesting history but it is not addressed at all
title: Saved by being short

body: We visited the tea factory early morning and got on one of the first tours. The guide was very motivated and passionate. He had competent answers too all questions asked.The factory is very interesting, it is fascinating to see older machinery (up to 70 years) still running (economically) in our time.The factory is located between very well maintained tea plantations and is also a lovely place for a picnic.For us one of the highlights in Nuwara Eliya.
title: Best Factory Tour we've been on for a while

body: Pedro is a very clean and well organized tea factory. The entry fee is LKR-200/- They first offer a a cup of tea which is followed by a 30 minutes tour of the factory going through the entire process of tea making. Factory is only in operation in night so during day visits the machines are not working. Factory also offers some good quality tea and souvenirs to sell. Along the factory are the tea plantations. You can visit them as well free of cost. There are no pictures allowed during the tour inside the factory but you can take pictures in the tea fields.
title: Very well managed

body: Excellent colonial factory and tea centre .Friendly staff who explained the tea making process and kids loved it .The tea served was super and a place you must take your kids to show the history of Sri Lankan tea and British influence .
title: Visit to Pedro tea factory

body: Interesting tour of factory costing 200rs, but for this you get cup of tea and more importantly they don't try and sell you anything else! Afterwards head back to entrance, grab since snacks from vendors outside and take the track opposite in order to head up to lovers leap waterfall. Takes about 30 mins to walk up there, follow the well trodden path through plantations for some excellent views of nuwara eliya and the waterfall itself
title: No forced sell

body: We came here based on the recommendation in our Lonely Planet guide. When we arrived, nobody greeted us or explained where to go for a tour. We were then told to 'hurry up and buy a ticket' as people were waiting for us. It turned out that a tour had already started, and they just made us join that one mid way through, which was a bit poor.However, the tour that we did see was very informative and interesting and it was nice to see the machines in action. Do bear in mind that no photos are allowed inside the factory.At the end of the tour, we were given a free cup of tea overlooking the plantation. The surrounding area is beautiful and I understand that not all tea factory tours have these sort of views.The shop was disappointing, so we went to the Blue Field Tea Factory shop on our way home to pick up some nicely packaged tea for gifts.Overall, it was a good place to get an understanding of the tea making process and sit and have a nice cup of tea with a great view.
title: Good tour and nice views

body: Went there on a Sunday with 3 friends. A lady guided us through the tea production process. However, the machinery was not functional which dampened the experience.I recommend going there on a fully functional day to get the best out of it. Its worth a trip.
title: Not fully functional on sundays

body: If you are spending one day in Nuwara Eliya and you would like to visit a tea plantation, you should come here.The tour lasts approximately 20 minutes and the entrance is only 200 rupees. We had a nice tour guide who explained us how the tea is produced and showed us all the machineries replying to all our questions. They also offer a cup of tea at the end of the visit.After the tour we had a walk around the estate, where we could take really nice pictures (inside the factory it is forbidden) of the plantation.
title: Interesting visit

body: Informative tour of quaint tea factory showing the process from picking to packaging and how the types of tea varieties are made. Had no idea that tea was processed so quickly and varieties all came from the same leaf. Just seeing the ancient machinery still being used is worth the visit. Tour finishes with a cup of tea adjacent to the shop.
title: Who knew tea was so quickly processed

body: OK we went on a Sunday so no work was happening but it was still a good little tour and you get told what each bit of equipment/room does. NO PHOTOS so be warned! Some girl in the group on the same tour as us kept trying to take them sneekily and the lady had a go at her, they get their wages docked if people take photos so don't do it!Good tour and then you get to have 1 cup of Lover's Leap tea after in their little sitting area bit, look or buy some tea if you want or a cup or something. Quite dear though but I am drinking the tea now at home and it is nice!
title: Amazing tea factory and lovely lady who did the tour

body: Nice quick tour of the simple factory, lovely estate area for some nice photos or to relax with your cup of tea after the tour well worth the trip out of town. Should prob be combined with a walk to lovers leap waterfall which is nearby. (1-2km).
title: Nice tea factory to visit. 200slr for 15mins and a cup of tea

body: Arrived at 3pm. Only two in my party but there were at least 15 in total on the tour. Guide was very clear, smiley and professional. Process made clear. Both my mum and I big tea drinkers so very interesting. Not a long tour, about 35 minutes. More would probably be boring and excessive! They mainly process the tea at night due to temperature, but the machines not being on doesn't matter at all. It gives you a clear view of the factory. Tea served was surprisingly nice as I've had some poor quality tea in Sri Lanka (the good stuff is exported!). A nice trip for the cost (200lkr). Grounds are pretty and you can walk around afterwards (it was raining so we didn't). Note: we haggled a tuktuk for 500 to take us from the Kelegala area, where our hotel was, to Pedro, then to the grand hotel. He wanted 1000 but we stuck to our guns, even walked away when he wouldn't go down. I know some may get it cheaper, but just for an idea of cost
title: Great info. All you need to know.

body: We arrived at 11am and the machines weren't working, however we were given a thorough tour of the tea factory costing 200r and lasting about 30 mins. Learnt much about how tea is picked, processed, manufactured and then graded and packed for sale and export all over the world. Both we and our teenage kids found it enjoyable and interesting. The tour ended up in the cafe overlooking the amazing estates, drinking a nice cup of BOPF- you'll know what this is after your visit !
title: Good Working Tea Factory

body: I recommend the visit to Pedro Tea Estate, the tour and the explanation about the process is quite short, but after you can enjoy a cup of tea while watching the magnificent views from there. Also very recommendable the walk to the Lovers Leap, just 5 km away.
title: Visit to the tea factory + Lovers Leap

body: Nice visit with one cup of tea offered, you will have to buy extra cups to do the easing of the 6 different teas.Try to be there before 11am to see all the machines working.
title: Interesting

body: A lovely place to visit and have some black tea. A factory is also available nearby which you can view. Note that they only sell black tea so if you want some of the more exquisite teas then I would recommend visiting some of the other tea fields in Nuwara Eliya. The best part of this tea estate is the view - and the fact that you can take a stroll in the tea fields - absolutely beautiful.
title: Warm black tea with views

body: Expected a more detailed explanation of the production cycle (very quick and high lavel) and a tour within the plantation (not done)
title: So and so

body: At the Pedro Estate we were offered a tour in the tea-factory which was very Interesting! There was a lot to learn about making all different kinds of tea. Also our teenage daughters loved this visit!
title: Interesting!

body: We visited on week day evening, they served us Hot Sri Lankan Tea with warm welcome for the factory tour. they gave us an whole idea about tea production. This is a must visit place in Nuwaraeliya.
title: Good Experience about Tea

body: We toured on Sunday so the factory was not operating but we still got a tour through and had explained to us how it all works. And a nice cup of tea at the end. Well worth it.
title: Enjoyable Tour

body: warm welcome and good explanation how tea is produced. The tea was tasted very good. Beautiful scenes and views. Large tea plantations.
title: Super tea production

body: Getting to one of the tea estate museums is well worthwhile - to learn something about the process of tea-making and why Ceylon tea is so famous. Great to see the tea plantations from close-up and to learn about the 24 hour process with sorting, cutting, drying, grading, packing and tasting... Surprised to learn that what I thought were different teas such as Pekoe or English Breakfast are the same tea cut and graded to different sized leaves. More subtle and feint honey coloured, the better - although many prefer darker stronger tea. What you won't learn about are worker conditions especially in the plantations and their homes - the lines - which have for centuries housed mostly Tamil labourer families. Fortunately some moves now being taken forward to improve conditions for these families and incorporate them more fully into Sri Lankan social and political life...
title: Worth a visit

body: Unfortunately I arrived at this place on a national holiday so the factory was not operating. However, it was open for a guided tour which proved highly informative and gave me a good insight into the process that provides us with our daily 'cuppa' . You get a free cup of tea at the end of the tour and the opportunity to purchase tea and related items, however I thought these were a bit overpriced.
title: Fascinating experience

body: Was given a very thorough and detailed tour of the factory by the very experienced staff. It was a wonderful tea making education that you can't get it anywhere. It is a must for anyone going up to the Nuwara Eliya region. The Lover Leap boutique is a nice touch. Don't miss the chance to have a go at picking tea leaves as well.
title: Fantastic vist

body: A nice tea factory to vissit. The sales women are eager to take you around and educate you on the process from picking of the tea leaves to drying and packaging and sampling. They have a store that sells you tea hampers
title: Tea Factory

body: Interesting tour by a lady who was able to answer all our questions about how tea is made. Tea is such a big part of Sri Lanka's economy so good to understand it a bit more. Tour didn't take long - about twenty minutes with opportunities to try and buy some local tea. Walked up to Lovers Leap afterwards
title: Good insight into tea production

body: It's all what we want to see when we are going there : - private visit of the factory (industrial -> so big volume) for 200 Rs- they explain the difference of black tea quality- you can go in the field- they offer you a cup of tea- you can buy tea souvenir
title: Good place to learn about TEA

body: in nuwara eliya there are many tea gardens . this is one of them . walk around and click good shots to take back memories home .
title: tes garden

body: There are many tea gardens in this area . So are the tea factories . They show you how tea is made . Than they make u taste tea . You can buy also.
title: Pedro tea factory

body: Pedro's is a great place to start your tea plantation education. The factory is one of 16 in the Kalani Valey group and for 200 rupees each you get a guided tour through the entire factory, a tea afterwards and access to the plantation fields to wander about in. After the ladies pluck the young tea leaves (the men do other heavier work, apparently), they are delivered to the factory. The machines they use to dry, roll, grind, and grade the tea are more than 80 years old. Quite a miracle. You get full access to all areas of production - but no photos inside. Pedro says it's an ethical company - they don't use chemicals, give all 1300 employees housing and have funds for medical benefits and schooling for the children of the staff. We bought a mixed box of six teas there for 1700 rupee which you can only get at the plantation. The rest is sent to Colombo for auction. We got a tuk tuk to take us to Pedro then Macwoods for 1300 rupee from Nuwara Eliya. Highly recommended.
title: Great insight to tea production

body: Very informative and enjoyable conducted factory tour first hand observation of the whole process from freshly plucked tea buds to final product packed and ready for the tea auction
title: Tour of tea processing factory

body: This is a great tour - you get to see a lot even though the machines only work at night time as they make a light tea.Very informative - great value
title: Very good tour

body: It was a Sunday and the Factory was closed but yet we were explained the process which was very instructive and worth the entry fee.
title: Fascinating insight how tea is made

body: The tea factory looks very 19th century. The tour cost 200 lkr and lasts about 15 minutes.The tea leaves arrive around noon, so before that you won't see any of the machines working. After noon the withering machine is supposed to work. The rest are only operational at night.Overall the tour was nice, but seeing working machines would be much better.The shop has a variety of expensive teas none of which are produced at the factory, since the factory doesn't do branding and packaging.The factory has a great view over the plantation.
title: Too bad the machines aren't working

body: Sri Lanka is famous for best tea in the world. You will be able to get good understanding of the tea making process from plucking the leaves to packaging. If machines are working then you will be able to see the whole process. You can select and buy processed tea starting from Rs. 250/- and each visitor is offered a fresh cup of tea. Mark this place a 'must go' in your places to visit in Nuwara Eliya.
title: How Sri Lankan Tea is Made !

body: The type of tea made here means that the whole process takes less than 24 hours - the withered leaves aren't fermented. Much of the processing is undertaken out of tourist opening hours. The brief tour is functional, but lacks the experience that comes from visiting a tea factory with all the machinery functioning, the heat and the smells. The first fresh leaves do not arrive until late morning, so best to avoid a visit before noon as even the dryers are empty and switched off. We were given a very clear instruction not to take photos, although it was unclear why. It is worth considering other tea factories for a fuller experience, but if this is your only chance to see a tea factory, then you will get an idea of how tea leaves are prepared for market.
title: limited experience of what a tea factory can offer

body: we enjoyed our visit to the tea factory. the staff work through the night so it was very quiet. We saw a few machines drying some of the tea leaves, and the rest were stationary. It was very interesting to see and hear how tea is made. You can buy from the little shop too - I think its a little expensive, but the boxes make nice gifts. Tuk Tuk drivers try to rip you off.. we paid 400 rupees (2 GBP), to go there and back from the city centre with him waiting. The tour takes about 10 minutes and costs 200 rupees (1GBP). You can walk through tea fields also.
title: a quick introduction to tea making.

body: The day we visited their machines were not working. They will still walk you through the manual process with a guide though no fun without looking at the entire process. They charge you LKR 200 per person which is pretty reasonable and includes a cup of tea. Even if you don't take the tour, you can have the tea for LKR 50. Best area to drink tea is to sit at the gallery.
title: Confirm if Machines are working

body: Oldest black tea factory in Sri Lanka. Good access and car park. Very nice view of tea farms. A very kind guide who show us all the factory and a great taste of sample tea...Must see
title: Real factory

body: I found the tour of this tea factory very interesting and informative but the tour guide was quite rude and she fed us a sob story before the tour of how the workers are underpaid etc (clearly looking for tips).Afterwards you get a cup of tea and can buy tea from the shop at a pretty reasonable price, but the selection is small.There was no work going on the day we arrived because it was full moon day but this did not really detract from the tour.The estate has lovely views and i would recommend walking or taking a tuktuk to lovers leap waterfall nearby.
title: Interesting tour, rude tour guide

body: We had a 30 minute tour, which was perfect. It was very interesting, shame we couldn't take photos inside the factory...but a good tour none the less.
title: Lovely to see a traditional tea factory!

body: It was fascinating to walk round the factory watching the production of 8 grades of tea and it's all done by hand with old fashioned machinery and not a computer in sight ! The final product is sold at auction to the big companies like Brooke Bond and Lipton who re-brand the tea and probably make a lot more money than the tea plantation and factory. It's lovely seeing the ladies out plucking the tea - a splash of colour in a sea of green.
title: Fascinating tour

body: We visited the Pedro factory after visiting Lover's Leap falls across the road. The tea they served us was over-brewed and bitter (even though it was their lighter tea). We paid for their factory tour which was a lot better than the one we went through at Mackwoods Labookellie tea centre. This tour was for over 30 mins and covered all processes of tea making, took us deep into the factory and showed us most of their machinery. Visit if you are interested in the tea process. Also, they don't sell a big variety of tea (unlike Mackwoods which has a huge collection) and most of their offerings are packets of 6 or so, hence you can't really pick and choose different varieties of tea.
title: Nice tour, not so nice tea

body: Slightly disappointing as the machinery was not working. we only had a guide, who was very good, but you did not get the feel of the produce being processed, felt all they wanted was you to spend money
title: the variety of tea
Worst out of the three main ones
body: This factory is the closest one from Nuwara Eliya, but its maybe the worst one, as it has sooo much publicity in all guide boooks and gets more touristy than the others. It is the only one that asks for entrance ticket (100), and offers same service - tour & cup of tea.

title: Nice to see a real factory in operation
body: While in tea country we visited Mackwoods and Pedros and enjoyed Pedros far more.We we taken into the production areas and saw everything up close and had an excellent guide who explained everything really well.Must admit the tea wasn't as good as Mackwoods though

title: Knowledgeable Place to visit
body: Really a Great Location With an Amazing view of the "Lovers Leap" Water fall. Surrounded by the Pedro Range Nuwara Eliya. Nearly 8km from the city center towards the Udapussallawa Road. 15mins Drive

title: Enjoyable visit
body: Having spent time in the area of tea plantations we were keen to see how tea was produced, our guide recommended Pedros to us, the factory tour covers the whole process from plant to finish product in great detail get to see all the processes at work. At the end you can sample the tea and wonder through some of the plantation, beautiful views.

title: Not as nice as Mackwoods Labookelie tea estate
body: We stopped here as this tea plantation is located across the road going up to the Lover's Leap falls.It can be easily and cheaply reached by taking the bus to Borlander.The grounds are not as nice as the ones at Mackwoods Labookelie.We did not do the tour as we have already done the one at Mackwoods Labookelie. They charge 200 rupees for the tour here.When we were leaving, we were lucky to see a large group of tea pickers returning to the plantation with their tea leaves baskets.

title: Very interesting
body: A few Kms outside the town. Our driver arranged a private guide to show us the production area which was fascinating and wonderful to be able to view the processes really up close. After a free cup of tea we were able to wander through the tea plantation which was so enjoyable. We happily bought a couple of packs of tea that has been produced on site. Very friendly people.

title: A lovely cuppa char!
body: We enjoyed our one hour visit to the tea factory. The young lady showing us what went on was delightful, although at times it was difficult to hear what she was saying because of the machinery noise. The view from the factory is spectacular. Well worth the time spent.

title: Great team! Marvellous General Manager.
body: We enjoyed the tea, we loved seeing the tea factory and bought gifts of superb tea for all at home. The estate GM was in at the time, frankly it was hard to believe that someone with so many staff could be welcoming and have so much time to chat. Big thanks! We will be back!

title: The best...
body: An interesting tour, a great explanation of the process. Make sure you take the time to stroll through the tea fields themselves.

title: A great visit
body: Insightful and interesting, quite well priced. Be sure to stroll through the tea plantations themselves.
